#5166. Bitmine Stock: Tom Lee Calls ETH ‘Hard Money’ – But BMNR Share Count Jumps 164%

Tom Lee calls Ethereum hard money as ETH supply growth stays near Bitcoin’s, but Bitmine’s 164% share dilution raises questions for BMNR investors.

Tom Lee made his “hard money” case for Ethereum (ETH) again this Week,  as Bitmine Immersion (BMNR) reported buying another 7,819 ETH last week. Bitmine stock rose 11% the same day, to $14.42, but is still down 44% in a month.

Lee’s argument is about supply. He said ETH’s supply has grown 0.90% a year since Bitmine started buying in June 2025, against 0.82% for Bitcoin (BTC). “In other words, ETH and BTC have essentially the same inflation rate, and both are ‘hard money’ measured in supply growth,” Lee said.

JUST IN: BitMine Immersion buys another 7,819 $ETH, bringing its total holdings to 6,085,564 ETH pic.twitter.com/2LZyEJyyBj

— Coingecko (@coingecko) November 23, 2026

We checked the numbers, and he is right about the coins, but the same test applied to Bitmine’s own shares tells a different story.

Lee’s numbers make a case for ETH as a coin that holds its value. But Bitmine shareholders do not own ETH directly. They own a slice of a company that keeps issuing new shares to buy more of it, and each new share dilutes that slice.

So does the hard-money case for ETH still hold for the people who own Bitmine stock, or is their share of Bitmine’s ETH being watered down faster than ETH’s supply grows?

Lee compared ETH with other big coins in Bitmine’s weekly update. Solana’s supply has grown 7.6% a year over the same period, XRP’s 5.4% and Cardano’s 2.9%, he said. “These others have been far more inflationary.”

Our own check, using CoinGecko’s daily circulating supply over the past 12 months, comes out almost the same:

Ethereum’s supply did grow about as slowly as Bitcoin’s over the past year. Most new ETH paid to validators is offset by the fees the network burns.

Market Intelligence: Crypto Analyst Reveals Upcoming Binance Listings

Bitmine paid for its ETH by printing shares. It had 232.4 million shares outstanding on August 31, 2025, and 613.3 million a year later, its annual report shows. By November 4, the count reached 626.5 million.

That is a 164% increase in one fiscal year, about 200 times ETH’s supply growth. Bitmine sold 395 million new shares through its at-the-market program in the Year to August, raising $12.9 billion.

Selling shares to buy ETH works for existing holders when the stock trades above the value of the coins behind it. It hurts when it trades below.

Right now, it trades below. Bitmine says its crypto, cash, and stakes are worth $11.1 billion, about $17.70 per share. At Monday’s close of $14.42, the market values Bitmine stock at roughly 0.81 times its assets, our estimate shows.

Bitmine has pushed back by buying its own shares. It repurchased 20.8 million shares at an average of $17 in July and August, and it has $3.6 billion left under its buyback plan.

EXPLORE: Ethereum News: BitMine To Halt Buying at 5% ETH Supply Cap

Bitmine now holds 6,085,564 ETH, or 4.98% of the 122.2 million in existence. Its stated goal is 5%, roughly 6.11 million ETH.

That leaves about 24,400 ETH to buy. At last week’s pace of 7,819 ETH, Bitmine would reach its target in about three weeks.

What happens after that matters for Bitmine stock. The weekly purchases have steadily driven demand for ETH, and Bitmine has said it would stop buying at 5%. With the stock below the value of its holdings, buybacks may use new money better than buying more ETH.

Most of the coins are already working. Bitmine stakes about 5.23 million ETH, 86% of its holdings, which it says earns about $245 million a year at current prices.

ETH trades at $1,698, below its 50-day exponential moving average (EMA), an average that gives recent prices more weight, at $2,113, and its 200-day EMA at $2,242.

Lee has made a fair case that ETH is as scarce as Bitcoin. For Bitmine stock, though, the share count matters as much as the coin count, and that has grown far faster.

While this comes as part of Ripple’s growing expansion into the traditional financial space, the blockchain firm announced it has partnered with Yapı Kredi, a major Turkish private bank, to support its cryptocurrency business.

As part of the partnership agreement, Ripple Custody will help the bank to securely manage its digital assets and provide custody services for its crypto trading platform dubbed Yapı Kredi Kripto.

While the partnership demands the full integration of the Ripple custodial infrastructure, the firm revealed that Ripple Custody will be installed on the bank's own premises.

The development is significant for the bank and the broader Turkish crypto market; it also marks a major milestone for Ripple as the firm claims to be the only custody service provider currently supporting leading Turkish banks licensed by the CMB as crypto asset custodians.

With Yapı Kredi now fortifying its position as a major player in Türkiye’s fast-growing crypto market, its partnership with the blockchain firm associated with XRP is likely to open new opportunities for XRP while positioning it for bigger adoption in the country.

Following the latest Ripple news, RLUSD (Ripple’s stablecoin) reached a new milestone over the weekend, with its circulating supply hitting a record $2.87 billion on Saturday, November 21. The surge also pushed RLUSD ahead of USD1, the stablecoin issued by the Trump family’s World Liberty Financial.

Ripple's $RLUSD hits a new all-time high of $2.874 billion in circulating supply, surpassing Trump's USD1 stablecoin.@Ripple pic.twitter.com/TlokhQ8Se8

— MSB Intel (@MSBIntel) November 23, 2026

The lead did not last, though. On Tuesday, RLUSD’s supply slipped to $2.82 billion, while USD1 held at about $2.85 billion.

The two coins are now separated by about $30 million, and they are heading in opposite directions. RLUSD has more than doubled in a year. USD1 has lost almost half its supply since February.

Meanwhile, XRP, the token closely tied to Ripple, trades near $0.93, down 26% this month.

So how did Ripple’s dollar catch up, and does it help XRP?

We pulled the daily supply of both coins from DefiLlama’s stablecoin dashboard, which adds up every chain they run on.

We also checked the contracts directly. RLUSD has $2.04 billion on Ethereum and $761 million on the XRP Ledger. USD1 is spread across BNB Chain ($1.10 billion), Solana ($868 million) and Ethereum ($852 million).

Market Intelligence: Crypto Analyst Predicts Next Crypto to Hit 1 Dollar

RLUSD’s growth has come in steps. Supply jumped from about $1.5 billion to $2.4 billion in August, then climbed again from late October.

Ripple has pushed it hard, and that push is behind most Ripple news this autumn. In October, the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency gave Ripple National Trust Bank final approval to manage RLUSD’s reserves. Robinhood expanded its RLUSD deal the same month. Binance has also run repeated campaigns that pay XRP to RLUSD holders.

USD1 is moving the other way. Its supply rose quickly early in 2026, then fell from $4.47 billion on October 7 to $2.85 billion now.

The XRP Ledger matters most for XRP holders. About $761 million of RLUSD sits there, roughly a quarter of the total. That is where RLUSD activity can create demand for XRP, which pays the ledger’s fees.

Bitcoin wallets could be linked to user IP addresses with 100% accuracy and for just about $0.34.

The flaw relies on the network's automatic rebroadcasting of small transactions that may have been out on hold by miners prioritizing higher fee transfers.

This is another in a recent line of Bitcoin vulnerabilities, including a hashrate hijacking spree and rumours of AI breaking ECC encryption.

According to Bitcoin Core contributor Abubakar Sadiq Ismail, the intrusion begins when an attacker sends low-fee ‘dust’ tokens to a BTC address.

Since miners prioritize higher-fee transactions, sending low amounts naturally takes longer time frames. The Bitcoin Core software automatically broadcasts stuck transactions after 12-36 hours, at which point an attacker is able to see the receiver’s IP address.

The method achieved a 100% success rate across 30 simulations on a regression test (regtest) network for only 18-34 cents per attempt.

At present, the flaw remains unpatched, and attackers are still able to get the exact location of Bitcoin wallets, in addition to viewing their balances.

And while no funds are at risk, such information could be used in crypto wrench attacks where an individual is physically targeted in a cryptocurrency robbery.

For now, Bitcoiners can choose manual wallet broadcasting in place of automatic broadcasts.

CoinPedia recently covered how attackers are hijacking Bitcoin hashrate, directing mining proceeds to their own wallets.

Even more, rumours still abound of OpenAI and Anthropic breaking several cryptographic security methods, including Elliptic Curve Cryptography, which Bitcoin relies upon.

The price of BTC remains unaffected by these reports, trading at around $60,000 for the last couple of days.

#5159. NEAR’s Inflation Cut: The Math Behind a 5.27% to 3.37% Staking Yield

AI-assisted summary, reviewed by NullTX editors.

HSP-029 lowers NEAR’s issuance cap from 2.5% to 1.6% over 24 months. The cap formula, the epoch step and the yield math show what that does to stakers.

Most headlines on NEAR’s new inflation schedule stop at “2.5% to 1.6%.” Stakers feel a different number. They earn about 5.27% today and will earn roughly 3.37% once the cut finishes, and a single line of arithmetic accounts for the gap.

House of Stake ratified HSP-029 on November 16, after the Security Council’s 14-day veto window passed without a veto. The proposal touches one parameter, the maximum annual issuance rate, which drops from 2.5% to 1.6% over 24 months. It is the second cut in just over a year, coming after the October 2025 halving from 5%.

Everything else stays put. Issuance still splits 90% to staking participants and 10% to the protocol treasury. There is no new spending program, no validator subsidy and no automatic trigger that could push issuance back up. The full proposal models 11.8 million NEAR of issuance avoided over two years and 66.1 million over six, measured against leaving the cap at 2.5%.

The schedule is a straight line with no stair steps:

Here t is the number of months since the reduction begins. The 0.9% is the total drop (2.5 minus 1.6), and dividing it by 24 gives a monthly step of 0.0375 percentage points, or 3.75 basis points. The min(t, 24) term caps the ramp at month 24, and the cap sits at 1.6% from there on.

NEAR applies the step every epoch rather than once a month. An epoch lasts about 12 hours, so the cap slips by roughly 0.0006 percentage points each time, far too little to notice on any given day. There are no step dates to mark on a calendar. Sampled every six months, the line looks like this:

The yield column uses the math in the next section. It drops about 0.08 percentage points a month, evenly, with no cliff.

New tokens go mostly to stakers, so the staked pool splits the reward, and a smaller pool earns more per token. That gives a working formula:

gross yield ≈ 0.9 × issuance cap ÷ staking ratio

The 0.9 is the staker share of issuance. Using the proposal’s figures, 0.9 × 2.5% ÷ 0.4271 comes to 5.27%, where 42.71% is the staking ratio reported when the proposal went to vote. Put in the 1.6% cap and 0.9 × 1.6% ÷ 0.4271 gives 3.37%, the same number the proposal publishes. Anyone can check the headline yields on a calculator.

The formula has two limits. It uses the cap, but realized issuance runs a little lower because transaction fees are burned. HSP-029 measured 2.45% in September, which puts today’s yield near 5.16%. The staking ratio also moves. When more people stake, the same rewards spread over more tokens and yield falls further, and when people unstake it climbs. The 3.37% figure assumes today’s ratio holds.

Stakers feel it first. By the proposal’s own math, someone staking 1,000 NEAR ends up with about 20 fewer tokens after two years than if the cap had stayed at 2.5%. The numbers back that up: yield averages about 4.32% across the ramp, roughly 0.95 points under today’s rate for two years.

Holders who don’t stake come out ahead. More than half of NEAR’s supply sits unstaked, and every new token dilutes those holdings. Trimming the cap by 0.9 percentage points trims that dilution by the same amount each year. Stakers give up some reward so that everyone else gives up less value.

Validators get an easier path than in 2025, when the halving cut staking rewards from about 9% to 4.75% in a single upgrade. Operators now have 24 months to plan. NEAR’s analysis finds that most validator revenue comes from commission on delegated stake, so service quality and fee competition shape income more than the issuance rate does.

Recent history explains the setup. When the 2025 halving shipped, an earlier community poll had missed the two-thirds threshold, and critics said the core team pushed the change through anyway. HSP-029 sidesteps that argument by design.

Two separate approvals are required. Token holders voting through veNEAR set the direction, and that vote closed November 2 with 99.96% in favor and none against. Validators then decide on their own whether to adopt the protocol upgrade that makes the cap binding. The author, Sal Ternullo of SVRN, opened discussion on October 7, and the process ran through the Screening Committee and Security Council in public. Raising issuance again would take a new proposal and another round of validator adoption, so nothing can be added quietly later.

Ratification does not change issuance yet. A one-quarter grace period comes first, giving wallets, exchanges, custodians and staking providers time to update their disclosures. NEAR One then releases the upgrade and validators choose whether to adopt it, with the reduction starting about a quarter after ratification. On schedule, that means a start in early 2027 and a 1.6% cap around early 2029.

Three things are worth tracking. Validator adoption of the upgrade comes first, because the cap stays at 2.5% until enough validators run it. The staking ratio comes next, since it moves yield regardless of the formula. Last are the quarterly transparency reports NEAR has promised, which compare realized issuance with the schedule.

Price is a separate question. Lower issuance eases supply pressure, but nothing in it creates demand. The cap will follow its published line down, and yield will follow the cap.

Zcash holders just got a new update as the major crypto exchange Gemini has announced support for Shielded Zcash deposits.

Scott Merkel, 'Wolf of All Streets,' shared this update in an X post, highlighting the milestone as the first of its kind for any major exchange. According to Merkel, Gemini now lets customers deposit Zcash (ZEC) to shielded addresses, saying it is the first major exchange with both shielded deposits and withdrawals.

GEMINI NOW LETS CUSTOMERS DEPOSIT ZCASH $ZEC TO SHIELDED ADDRESSES, SAYING IT IS THE FIRST MAJOR EXCHANGE WITH BOTH SHIELDED DEPOSITS AND WITHDRAWALS https://t.co/d9pIFJ6uJM

Gemini co-founder Tyler Winklevoss shared the milestone in a recent X post, adding that the recent move builds on the launch of shielded Zcash withdrawals on Gemini this summer.

In July 2026, shortly after the Ironwood upgrade was activated, Gemini launched support for shielded Zcash withdrawals to the new Ironwood pool, allowing users to send Zcash from Gemini to their Ironwood deposit address. Ironwood (NU6.3) went live on July 28, 2026, at block height 3,428,143, bringing a new shielded pool for Zcash.

With the recent launch of support for Shielded Zcash deposits, Gemini users can make Shielded Zcash deposits and withdrawals to and from Ironwood, with Winklevoss remarking that the private movement of money was now complete.

Zcash's total shielded supply now sits at around 4.93 million ZEC (around 28.94% of total ZEC supply) as of November 25, 2026.

November has brought in key updates for the Zcash network. Zcash's NU7 upgrade went live earlier in November 2026, slashing ZEC's target block time to 25 seconds from 75 seconds. The new 25-second block target lets miners add a batch of transactions to the chain three times as often.

None of this prints extra ZEC. Each block pays a third as much and halvings come every 5,040,000 blocks instead of 1,680,000, so the issuance schedule holds at roughly four years per halving.

Days after the NU7 upgrade, the Zcash Foundation followed up with the release of Zebra 7.1.0, which fixed ten security advisories, most of which closed off ways in which another node on the network (a peer) could stop a Zebra node from catching up with the chain or make it run out of memory. It also added sync and memory diagnostics, automatic peer recovery, and clearer errors.

#5156. JPMorgan, HSBC and StoneX Trade Digital Gold in London as Tokenized Gold Holdings Jump 48%

London is testing tokenized gold as Tether Gold and PAX Gold holdings climb 48% to $4.6 billion despite falling gold prices.

JPMorgan, HSBC and StoneX completed the first live wholesale trades of fractional tokenized gold in London last week. The test is meant to keep the world’s largest gold market ahead of Asian rivals. The three firms also used the digital gold as collateral, without moving a single bar out of the vaults.

Bloomberg reported the trades on Tuesday. They ran on a system built by the World Gold Council (WGC), the industry body that led the project. David Tait, the WGC’s chief executive, called it “a historic step forward for the gold market.”

JPMORGAN $JPM, HSBC AND STONEX COMPLETE THE FIRST LIVE WHOLESALE TRADES OF FRACTIONAL DIGITAL GOLD IN LONDON, ALSO USING IT AS COLLATERAL pic.twitter.com/bwVAdrpkXh

— The Wolf Of All Streets (@scottmelker) November 24, 2026

The banks did not say how much gold changed hands. The system is still in testing, and there is no date yet for a wider launch. The timing is awkward for gold itself. The metal trades near $3,626 an ounce, 32% below its January record and 11% lower than a year ago.

What changes for London’s bullion market, and does it matter for crypto’s own gold tokens?

The WGC calls the new format “pooled gold interests.” Each one is a fractional, electronically transferable share in a pool of physical bars held in approved London vaults.

That fills a gap. Most London trades today are in unallocated gold, which is cheap to hold but leaves buyers as creditors if their bank fails. Allocated gold means owning specific bars, which is safer but costly and hard to split. The WGC proposed the pooled model with law firm Linklaters in September 2025 as a third route between the two.

The collateral piece matters most. Banks could pledge gold for loans and margin as easily as they post bonds, without trucks or vault transfers.

London has a lot riding on it. Its over-the-counter market handles more than $180 billion of gold trades a day, and its vaults held $1.4 trillion of gold in August. Hong Kong, working with the Shanghai Gold Exchange, began testing its own gold clearing system in July.

Market Intelligence: Crypto Analyst Predicts Best Low-Cap Crypto

The London pilot is a closed, bank-only system. Crypto has run its own version for years with Tether Gold (XAUT) and PAX Gold (PAXG), and those tokens have been growing fast.

We read the supply of both tokens straight from their Ethereum contracts, where each token equals one troy ounce. We compared that with CoinGecko’s figures from a year ago.

So crypto’s digital gold kept adding ounces even as the gold price fell. Still, the two tokens hold about 0.33% of the value of gold sitting in London’s vaults. The whole tokenized gold category traded about $329 million in the past 24 hours on CoinGecko, against London’s $180 billion a day.

Explore: RLUSD Surpasses Trump’s USD1 Stablecoin but XRP Still Sinks 26%

PAX Gold tracks the metal closely. On Binance, PAXG trades at $3,637, below its 50-day exponential moving average (EMA), an average that gives recent prices more weight, at $3,945, and its 200-day EMA at $4,195.

Last week’s sell-off pushed it to $3,491 on Saturday, its lowest level in 300 days. Sellers led on Binance’s spot market, where the token itself changes hands. Orders that sold at the market price right away outweighed buyers by a net $13.4 million over the past seven days.

Market Intelligence: Crypto Analyst Reveals Upcoming Coinbase Listings

The WGC still has to settle governance rules and a launch date. If the big banks adopt digital gold for collateral, the gap between London’s vaults and crypto’s gold tokens could start to close.

#5155. Why Does AI Get Simple Questions Wrong? What Google's Humanity's First Exam Shows

You ask an AI model to name the color of the third letter in each word on a neon sign. It gets it right. You ask again, and it slips by one letter. Nothing broke.

The model could do the task. It just did not do it every time. Google DeepMind built a test for exactly that gap, and the results show how far "usually right" can sit from "reliably right."

Most AI benchmarks ask a model to solve a hard problem once. If it passes, it scores. Google DeepMind's Humanity's First Exam (HFE), released on November 24, 2026, asks something different. Can a model solve an easy task, and slight rewrites of it, every single time?

The prompts are elementary on purpose. They cover counting objects, naming colors, tracking where something moved, basic arithmetic, strict formatting rules and spotting false premises. Humans solve them in about a minute.

One public example: "List the color of the third letter of each word in the neon sign in order, separated by a semicolon." The answer is green; yellow; white; blue; blue.

The paper calls the difference the Family Reliability Gap. One slip anywhere in the 16 answers fails the whole family.

The top five models score 96% to 98% on a single try and 100% on family pass@4. Their family pass⁴ averages only 85.8%. Across all 18 models, the gap runs from 7.6 to 80.1 percentage points.

The bottom row is the sharpest case. That model gets 68.7% of single tries right, yet clears only 18.6% of question families every time. Its family pass@4 is 98.8%, so it could solve nearly every family at least once.

The math is simple. Say a model is right 90% of the time on each answer, and the answers are independent. Getting 16 in a row right happens about 18.5% of the time (0.9 to the 16th power). That is a rough illustration, not the paper's calculation, but it shows how small error rates compound.

The paper's own example makes the same point. One model trails the leader by 6.6 points on single tries and by 29.4 points on family pass⁴. On average, about half the shortfall comes from prompts a model always fails. The other half comes from flakiness: right on some runs, wrong on others.

Humans and models also struggle in opposite places. People were least accurate on math and logic seeds. Models were strongest there and weakest on counting and reading text inside images.

Traders now hand AI tools real jobs: reading a contract, summarizing a token page, checking a wallet address in a screenshot, or running a bot. In those jobs, one wrong character or one miscounted number is the whole failure. A model that is right 19 times out of 20 will still be wrong on the 20th, and a signed transaction cannot be undone.

1. Ask twice. Run the same question more than once. If the answers differ, treat both as unconfirmed.

2. Check the visual parts yourself. Counts, colors, positions and text read from an image are where models slip most. Compare addresses and numbers character by character against the original.

3. Match the effort to the task. More reasoning helps with text and math. It helps little with images, so do not assume a longer "thinking" mode makes a screenshot read safe.

4. Keep a human on irreversible steps. Sending funds, signing transactions and changing settings should not rest on a single AI answer.

#5153. XRP Exchange Inflows Hit 4.61 Billion in 30 Days

XRP has continued to see traders deposit large amounts of tokens into exchanges, including Binance, Bybit and others, as the prolonged market volatility has triggered increased fear across the broader crypto market.

Latest data from the crypto analytics platform CryptoQuant shows that about 4.61 billion XRP have flowed into crypto exchanges over the last 30 days.

According to the data, Binance has led all other crypto exchanges in the amount of XRP inflows received over the last month as its users appear to have panicked amid rising market struggles.

As such, Binance recorded about 1.221 billion XRP deposits during the period, representing the lion's share of the total inflows.

Ranking second on the list is OKX, which followed with about 866.51 million XRP, while Bybit was next with 662.57 million XRP.

The trend extended to other exchanges, even though they saw considerably lower inflows: Upbit saw about 176.96 million XRP flow into its exchange during the same period, while Bitget recorded inflows of about 140.02 million XRP.

Although the past month has seen billions of XRP transferred back to exchanges, further data shows that the 4.6 billion XRP inflow is substantially lower when compared with inflows seen in October.

In October, the total XRP that flowed into exchanges throughout the month was estimated at around 6 billion XRP, suggesting that XRP selling pressure has eased compared with the previous month.

This has drawn attention across the crypto market as the price of XRP suffered larger losses this month compared with last month, sparking questions about whether investor confidence is recovering.

Most of the crypto-related positions in the filing are Bitcoin products and Bitcoin-linked stocks, and the bank also reported a small amount of XRP exposure through three spot exchange-traded funds.

The largest crypto-related position in the filing is Strategy (MSTR). Morgan Stanley held around 10.88 million MSTR shares worth about $1.67 billion at the end of September, up from 9.33 million shares at the end of the second quarter.

Before that, the bank's first-quarter filing showed 1,700 shares of the Volatility Shares XRP ETF and 100 shares of the Grayscale XRP Trust ETF worth $15,488 in total.

#5151. French Senate Rejects Disclosure Rule for Crypto

French senators on Nov. 24 rejected a proposal that would have required taxpayers to disclose self-hosted cryptocurrency holdings exceeding €100,000.

They would have had to report those assets as of Dec. 31.

This would have been the case even if they had held the same coins since January without making any sales.

Two matching amendments to the French 2027 budget were rejected by the Senate during the first reading of the draft.

Senators Pascal Savoldelli and Anne-Sophie Romagny reintroduced the proposal after it briefly passed in the National Assembly earlier in the month.

French taxpayers must disclose their crypto assets held on foreign crypto platforms.

These amendments would have expanded disclosure requirements to wallets that owners directly control. This pertains to a wallet that is not managed by an exchange or another custodian.

The French National Assembly approved the €100,000 disclosure threshold in a 150-44 vote on Nov. 3. There were also eight abstentions.

The next day, the National Assembly voted down the entire revenue portion of the budget.

This vote brought down the wallet disclosure provision along with the rest of the budget.

However, the subsequent effort to revive the provision in the Senate was defeated.

It should be noted that the 2027 budget is still being considered at the time of writing.

The Senate also rejected two other crypto-related measures debated as part of the budget.

One was a provision to tax gains realized when holders exchange cryptocurrencies for certain stablecoins.

The second was a proposal to expand France's exit tax to include unrealized gains on cryptocurrencies held by taxpayers who move their tax residence outside the country.

#5145. Bitcoin Price Could Crash to $39K Despite Slowing ETF Outflows: Is Worst Yet to Come?

ETF outflows are slowing, but historical cycles and the 0.786 Fibonacci level point to a potential BTC bottom between $39,000 and $44,000.

In Bitcoin news this week, the selling from US spot Bitcoin ETFs is easing, but the price has not followed. On Tuesday, November 24, the funds lost a net $232 million. That was less than half of Monday’s $570 million.

It was still the sixth day of outflows in a row. The funds have shed about $2.6 billion since November 17 and nearly $5 billion this month, led by BlackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT).

Bitcoin spot ETFs have recorded SIX consecutive trading sessions of net outflows, with approximately 41,540 BTC withdrawn over that period.

The latest session saw another 3,780 BTC leave the funds, bringing further pressure on institutional demand.

BlackRock's IBIT accounted… pic.twitter.com/PUKLdaUgKS

— CryptoSavingExpert ® (@CryptoSavingExp) November 25, 2026

Bitcoin keeps sliding anyway. It trades near $58,900 on Wednesday, down 53% from its October 2025 record of $126,272. On Saturday, it touched $55,081, its lowest price in more than two years.

So if the funds are selling less, where could Bitcoin’s bear market end? We checked where Bitcoin bottomed in every past cycle, using Fibonacci retracement levels, ratios traders use to measure how much of a rally gets erased.

SoSoValue’s ETF flow figures, as reported this week, show the pressure easing:

Even after the selling, the funds still hold about $52 billion of net inflows since launch. That is roughly 83% of their October 2025 peak, so most ETF buyers have not left.

For Bitcoin news readers, slower outflows don’t mean buyers are back, though. They mean less forced selling from one big source. For the price to turn, the flows need to flip to inflows.

Market Intelligence: Crypto Analyst Predicts Best New Crypto to Hodl

Fibonacci retracements measure how much of a rally a market gives back. Traders watch a handful of ratios, mainly 0.618 and 0.786, as places where a drop may stop.

We measured each Bitcoin cycle on Bitstamp’s daily price history since 2011. Each runs from one bear-market bottom to the next record high. We then checked how much of that move was erased by the next bottom.

That is the less-reported Bitcoin news: each bear market stopped a little earlier than the last, by three to four points each time. If that trend holds, the next bottom would land near the 0.786 Fibonacci level, a 78.6% retracement.

This cycle runs from the 2022 low of $15,479 to the $126,272 record. On that range, 0.786 sits at about $39,200. So far, Bitcoin has given back 64.3%. Saturday’s low already cut through the 0.618 level at $57,800.

A log scale treats a doubling the same at any price. On that scale, past bottoms came at shallower ratios, rising from 33% to 48%. The 0.5 level on that scale for this cycle is about $44,200. Both methods point to a $39,000 to $44,000 zone.

Bitcoin trades at $58,930 on Binance, below its 50-day exponential moving average (EMA), an average that gives recent prices more weight, at $71,954, and its 200-day EMA at $74,702.

Market Intelligence: Crypto Analyst Predicts Best Low-Cap Crypto

The Bitcoin news to watch is the ETF flow data. A first day of inflows would be the clearest sign the selling is done. Until then, past cycles say the bottom could still be well below today’s price.

Gold’s historic rally has turned into one of the year’s sharpest commodity reversals. After reaching record levels above $5,500 in January, the precious metal has surrendered a substantial portion of its gains, with prices briefly falling below $3,500 in November. The correction has raised concerns about whether the long-running gold bull market has entered a deeper downturn.

Rising interest-rate expectations, a stronger US dollar and weakening investment demand are creating fresh challenges for bullion, while historical market cycles offer a warning about the potential duration of major corrections.

Gold’s decline has reversed a significant part of the rally that pushed prices to record levels earlier this year. Bullion reached an all-time high near $5,595 per ounce in January before entering a prolonged correction.

Gold's biggest historical crashes are flashing a terrifying warning.Gold has crashed nearly 37% from its 2026 all-time high, after one of the biggest rallies in its history.And something similar has happened after previous major gold bull markets.• 1970–1980: Gold surged… pic.twitter.com/nCnyiH0P1a

The correction has revived comparisons with previous gold bull markets. Historical cycles show that powerful rallies can be followed by extended periods of losses and sideways trading.

For example, the 1970s bull market was followed by a severe correction that kept gold below its previous peak for decades. Similarly, after the 2011 peak, bullion did not establish a sustained move to a new record until 2020.

These comparisons highlight the risks of buying near market peaks. However, the size and duration of previous corrections should not be treated as a forecast for the current cycle. Monetary policy, central-bank demand and global investment conditions are different across each period.

The biggest pressure on gold has come from changing expectations around US monetary policy. Persistent inflation has strengthened expectations that the Federal Reserve could raise interest rates again. Higher yields make interest-bearing assets such as Treasury securities more attractive relative to gold, which does not generate income.

The US dollar has also added pressure. Since international gold prices are denominated in dollars, a stronger greenback makes bullion more expensive for buyers using other currencies and can weaken demand.

Recent market developments have reinforced these concerns. Gold fell below $3,500 on November 25 as investors responded to stronger inflation pressures and expectations of further Fed tightening. The metal remained under pressure the following day, before recovering on November 27.

The broader market environment has also contributed to selling. During periods of market stress, investors sometimes liquidate gold positions to raise cash or cover losses elsewhere, weakening its traditional safe-haven appeal.

Gold’s price chart shows a clear deterioration in its technical structure. After reaching its January peak, the metal formed a sequence of lower highs and lower lows, with selling pressure becoming more pronounced in November. The asset price has also moved below its short- and long-term moving averages. These indicators are now positioned above the current price, suggesting that buyers face multiple resistance barriers before a sustained recovery can develop.

The latest rebound from the November low offers some relief, but it has not yet reversed the broader downtrend. A sustained move above the short-term moving averages would be an initial signal that selling pressure is easing. However, failure to hold the recent recovery could bring the November low back into focus.

A decisive break below that area would increase downside risks, while a stronger recovery accompanied by improving momentum could help gold establish a more stable base.

Historical corrections show why investors should be cautious after an unusually strong rally. Gold’s previous major peaks were followed by lengthy recovery periods, leaving investors who bought near those highs waiting years to regain their positions.

The current correction raises a similar question, particularly as higher interest rates challenge the investment case for a non-yielding asset. However, gold’s long-term outlook also depends on factors beyond US interest rates. Central-bank purchases, geopolitical uncertainty, currency diversification and renewed demand for safe-haven assets could support prices if macroeconomic conditions change.

Gold’s November rebound has provided some relief, but the broader technical structure remains under pressure. Investors will closely monitor US inflation data, Treasury yields, dollar movements and Federal Reserve signals for clues about the next direction.

If rate-hike expectations continue to strengthen, gold could face further selling pressure. A shift toward a less restrictive monetary outlook, combined with renewed investment demand, could support a more durable recovery.

The key question is whether November’s correction marks a temporary reset after an extraordinary rally or the beginning of a longer consolidation cycle. For now, gold needs stronger buying momentum to demonstrate that its latest rebound can develop into a sustained recovery.

#5140. Ukraine Legalizes Crypto After One-Day Delay

Home » Regulations » Ukraine Legalizes Crypto After One-Day Delay

Crypto-embracing Bill No. 10225-d gets the highest-priority treatment following a slight procedural delay.

Ukraine’s parliament has approved a bill to bring cryptocurrency trading, custody and taxation under a formal legal framework.

The measure, Bill No. 10225-d, passed after lawmakers postponed consideration a day earlier, a pause that had raised questions about its immediate path despite renewed support from the parliamentary finance committee for the revised text.

The Ukraine crypto bill is designed to legalize and regulate the domestic virtual-asset market rather than leave it in a largely undefined legal space.

Its scope includes tax treatment for crypto activity as well as rules for trading platforms and custodial services.

That approach would place businesses handling customer assets under a clearer licensing and compliance structure.

BREAKING: Ukraine officially passes law to LEGALIZE crypto, effective July 1, 2027. pic.twitter.com/6KxnNa7N2b

The framework comes into practice on July 1, 2027. It offers more certainty over how digital-asset transactions are treated by authorities, though implementation details will matter as much as the legislation itself.

Ukraine has maintained an active crypto sector despite the strains of war, with digital assets playing a visible role in fundraising and cross-border transfers.

Formalizing the market has therefore carried significance beyond ordinary financial regulation: it could help define how crypto businesses operate in an economy still managing exceptional pressures with the fifth year of war with Russia coming along.

The Ukraine crypto bill’s journey shows how quickly crypto policy can shift even when lawmakers broadly support regulation.

BREAKING: Zelensky President of Ukraine officially legalizes Bitcoin & crypto after parliament passes the bill with 271 vote pic.twitter.com/qt9C7jcNVK

The November 24, 2026 postponement followed committee backing for a revised version, while the subsequent passage points to a resolution of at least some of those immediate obstacles.

Questions remain over the final tax mechanics, the timing of licensing requirements and which agencies will oversee different parts of the sector. Market participants will also watch for secondary rules that determine the practical burden on exchanges, brokers and wallet providers.

Ukraine’s crypto move matters because it adds another sizable European market pursuing rules for digital assets rather than relying on prohibition or legal ambiguity.

The Ukraine crypto legislation may give local firms a route toward greater legitimacy, but the ultimate test will be whether the resulting framework is workable enough to retain innovation while improving crypto oversight.

#5137. Ethereum maps post-AI, post-quantum cryptographic overhaul with Keccak-256 — Details

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

Ethereum Foundation is in the news today after it announced that it has recommended Keccak-256 as the hash function for Ethereum’s hash-based cryptography.

The ongoing bear market price action is only a bump in the road. In the long term, however, the network has to be prepared to contend with threats posed by both quantum computing and progressing artificial intelligence capabilities.

On Tuesday, 24th November, the Foundation revealed its recommendation and the reasons behind it.

It considered five candidates: the ZK-friendly hashes, Poseidon and Poseidon2, the fast hashes BLAKE3 and BLAKE2, and the two hashes Ethereum already uses- SHA-256 and Keccak-256.

Keccak-256 has “arguably the most extensive cryptanalysis out of all unbroken traditional hashes,” the blog post read. An additional benefit is that this hash function has so far remained unaffected by AI-assisted cryptanalysis

Zero-knowledge proof technology improvements have removed the performance advantages offered by Poseidon. Security was the primary concern.

Though natively fast, the best collision attack reached 38 out of 64 rounds for SHA-256. Only 5 out of 24 rounds were reached for Keccak-256.

The Foundation also recommended against using SHA3-256 alongside Keccak-256 since both use the same underlying permutation and have similar security characteristics.

According to Ethereum Foundation Researcher Kev Wedderburn, they have been planning ways to counter quantum computing’s threat. In fact, AI has emerged as a more urgent risk recently.

Models are already finding bugs in production software faster than people can review them, the researcher wrote.

The planned upgrade will overhaul how validators sign messages, users authorize transactions, and how Ethereum verifies data posted by rollups.

It is harder than the 2022 Merge, and there is less time, Wedderburn acknowledged. Working faster can ship more bugs, so the Foundation has doubled the protocol security team to ensure formal verification. This will also allow the security work to progress at the pace of protocol development.

#5134. Switzerland’s First Spot Bitcoin ETF BBIT Begins Trading on SIX

Home » Bitcoin (BTC) » Switzerland’s First Spot Bitcoin ETF BBIT Begins Trading on SIX

BIT Asset Management’s regulated fund brings direct spot Bitcoin access to Swiss retail accounts.

BIT Asset Management’s Bitcoin Fund ETF (BBIT), Switzerland’s first spot Bitcoin exchange-traded fund, began trading on the SIX Swiss Exchange on November 26, 2026. Structured as a regulated Swiss collective investment fund, the product gives retail investors direct Bitcoin exposure through standard Swiss bank or brokerage accounts without self-custody.

The passive fund tracks the SIX Bitcoin Reference Rate and holds physical Bitcoin offline in cold storage at regulated Swiss custodian AMINA Bank AG, ring-fenced from the manager’s and custodian’s own assets.

BIT Asset Management describes BBIT as Europe’s currently active spot Bitcoin ETF, though public offering is approved only in Switzerland.

BBIT is listed on SIX Swiss Exchange and trades in both U.S. dollars and Swiss francs, with a target annual management fee of 0.19%. The fund launched with an initial issue price of $10 per unit and an allocation of 350 BTC, valued at more than $20 million at launch.

Switzerland’s Financial Market Supervisory Authority (FINMA) approved BBIT’s fund contract on October 20, 2026, following an 18-month review.

FINMA granted an exemption from standard investment diversification requirements, allowing the fund to invest exclusively in Bitcoin based on the cryptocurrency’s established trading history and liquidity.

However, the fund is classified as an alternative investment fund with specific risks, reflecting Bitcoin’s volatility and potential for substantial capital losses.

Unlike most European crypto exchange-traded products, which are structured as debt instruments and expose investors to issuer credit risk, BBIT operates under Swiss collective investment scheme legislation. This means investors hold fund units backed by ring-fenced assets, legally separated from the fund management company’s own assets.

Pernet von Ballmoos AG (PvB) acts as the fund management company and issuer, while BIT Asset Management serves as the sponsor and investment manager. Flow Traders has been appointed as the market maker, supporting secondary-market liquidity.

The fund also provides daily disclosure of its Bitcoin holdings and supports in-kind subscriptions for eligible institutional participants.

While BBIT is Switzerland’s first retail spot Bitcoin ETF, a physically backed Bitcoin product—the Jacobi FT Wilshire Bitcoin ETF—previously debuted on Euronext Amsterdam in August 2023 before Euronext listed it as inactive in February 2026 and liquidation proceedings began later that month. Meanwhile, SIX has hosted physically backed crypto ETPs since 2019.

The listing arrives with Bitcoin price hovering near $60,500 after heavy November outflows across U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs.

BIT—formerly known as Matrixport—expanded its Swiss fund footprint after acquiring and rebranding its Swiss asset management arm (originally rooted in Crypto Finance Asset Management).

This approval is a major step for Switzerland, as it allows everyday investors to gain direct exposure to Bitcoin through a regulated Swiss investment fund. It also shows that regulators are becoming more open to Bitcoin as a mainstream investment asset.

#5132. Bitcoin ‘As Important as It’s Ever Been’ if Inflation Rises, Coinbase CEO Says

"Bitcoin investors tend to sell BTC when there's a big IPO. Then they come back."

That's Coinbase CEO Brian Armstrong's take on Bitcoin investor behavior, less than a week after the record-breaking $93.5 billion IPO of Claude creator Anthropic.

"Historically, people rotate out of it to take advantage of a big IPO. Then they come back in," Armstrong wrote on X earlier today.

The limited window of opportunity to invest in an IPO helps explain the behavior Armstrong described. For an investor to buy at the IPO price, there's only a certain period during which they can request an allocation of shares. After that, the price is determined by the market.

On Nov. 19, Anthropic went public on the Nasdaq, and that brief window of opportunity mattered.

Shares were priced at $83, up from the $70-$78 range indicated just two days earlier. Anthropic's stock, trading under the ticker ANT, opened at $111.50.

If you bought at that opening price, you paid about 34% more per share than an investor who received an allocation at the IPO price.

When the IPO closed on Nov. 20, 1.127 billion shares had been sold, including 147 million additional shares purchased by underwriters exercising their option.

Of the $93.5 billion in gross proceeds, Anthropic itself received around $91.6 billion. The rest went to existing shareholders.

There was also a separate $26 billion private placement involving investors such as Microsoft, Nvidia, Google and others. In total, the combined transactions were valued at $119.5 billion.

As for the longer-term case for holding BTC, Armstrong's point concerns investors' expectations about the future purchasing power of their money.

"If you think there is going to be more inflation and money printing in the future, bitcoin is as important as ever."

At the heart of the matter is Bitcoin's 21 million supply limit.

If you expect governments to continue expanding the money supply, you may still be excited by the prospect of a major IPO. And you may sell some of your BTC to participate in it.

Armstrong's argument is that the window of opportunity to participate in a major IPO eventually closes.

However, the reasons investors bought Bitcoin in the first place may remain long after the newly listed stock starts trading.

#5130. MetaMask Brings Stablecoin Payments to Three Asian Markets With New Card Launch

Home » Blitz news » MetaMask Brings Stablecoin Payments to Three Asian Markets With New Card Launch

MetaMask expands its payment card to Japan, Thailand, and Vietnam for Mastercard transactions.

Cryptocurrency wallet provider MetaMask launched its payment card in Japan, Thailand and Vietnam on November 25, allowing users to spend its dollar-pegged mUSD stablecoin at merchants that accept Mastercard.

The move gives users in the three markets another way to use stablecoins for everyday purchases. Rather than transferring funds to a centralized cryptocurrency exchange before spending them, users can make payments directly through a card linked to their MetaMask wallet.

MetaMask Card uses mUSD, a US dollar-pegged stablecoin, to make payments at merchants that accept Mastercard. Users can pay online with their virtual card or in stores through Apple Pay and Google Pay. At checkout, the required amount of mUSD is converted into the local currency, such as Japanese yen.

In Japan, the card is available only as a virtual version and carries no annual fee. ATM cash withdrawals are not supported. Users can spend up to $10,000 per transaction and $15,000 per day.

Payments made with an mUSD balance at domestic merchants carry no transaction fee, while purchases at merchants outside the user’s country of residence incur a 1% fee.

To apply, users must access the Money tab in the MetaMask mobile app, register an email address and phone number, complete identity verification (KYC), and provide proof of residence.

However, the card does not support direct payments with every cryptocurrency held in MetaMask. Users must first convert assets such as USDC into mUSD before adding funds to their MetaMask Money account.

The Japanese cards are issued by New Zealand-based financial services provider Immersve Limited. MetaMask says its Money account retains a self-custodial structure, allowing users to maintain control of their private keys.

The expansion comes as stablecoin activity continues to grow across Southeast Asia, where digital assets are increasingly used for cross-border payments and transfers.

Chainalysis’s 2026 regional research shows that Thailand and Vietnam, alongside the Philippines, accounted for 14.4% of global small-value peer-to-peer transfers. The report also found that cross-border stablecoin activity exceeded domestic volumes in both countries, reaching $10.4 billion in Thailand and $6.9 billion in Vietnam.

Japan offers a different opportunity. Its developing regulatory framework and growing interest in stablecoins provide another market for MetaMask to test whether crypto wallets can become practical payment tools.

MetaMask first tested its payment card in the UK and Europe in August 2024 before launching it to US customers in February 2026. The service has since expanded to the European Economic Area, Canada, and parts of Central and South America.

Crypto has an AI sector of its own, and from the outside it looks like one trade. Up close, the projects in it do very different jobs, and a comparison only makes sense once you know which job each one does.

Part of the sector already earns real revenue. Venice, a private AI app, became a unicorn in July 2026 with a $65 million Series A, and its CEO, Erik Voorhees, told TechCrunch that the company is profitable, with annualized run-rate revenues of over $70 million. People pay for private AI.

The map goes layer by layer, and each project is described from its own site.

The base layer connects idle graphics cards with the people who need them.

Most of what this layer sells is time on hardware, though Akash and io.net now also sell access to open models through APIs. For teams weighing a rented GPU against their own hardware, Lightchain AI has published a comparison of self-hosting an LLM and a worker network.

Here the network itself decides whose work is best, and pays for it.

This layer competes with ChatGPT on the user’s side of the screen.

Lightchain is building an agents layer of its own, Lightchain Agents, with a waitlist open now.

This is where Lightchain AI sits. It is a layer-1 blockchain built to run AI. Its blog keeps a plain list of what is live on the network today.

Lightchain also touches three of the other layers:

The sector will keep trading as one theme. It works more like a stack, where each layer needs the others: GPUs to run on, models worth running, apps people want, agents that act, and a record that shows what happened. Lightchain’s bet is on that last layer: the more AI runs on open networks, and the more agents pay one another, the more a public record of who served each answer matters.

Lightchain AI is a layer-1 blockchain for AI. Independent operators stake LCAI and serve open models such as gpt-oss, Qwen3, and Llama from their own GPUs. The chain assigns each job, holds the fee in escrow, and keeps a record of every job that anyone can look up. Products live today include Lightchain Chat, Lightchain Desktop (beta), Lightchain Studio, the Lightchain Bridge, and the Lightscan explorer. The LCAI DUNA, a Wyoming association, is the project’s legal entity.

#5127. CZ Urges 1Password Users to Change All Their Passwords

After a hacker stole customer data, Binance founder Changpeng Zhao advised 1Password users to change all the passwords stored in the service.

1Password offered different advice about what users should do after the incident was disclosed on Nov. 25. The password management service said hackers hadn't gained access to the passwords stored in users' vaults, so there was no need to reset them.

"If you use 1Password, recommend you to change ALL your passwords. It's a pain in the neck, but necessary," Zhao said on X, replying to a post from Coin Bureau about the breach.

If you have a crypto exchange login stored in 1Password, this distinction is important.

1Password says hackers could access the email address a customer uses to log in to the service. But they couldn't see the exchange password saved in the customer's vault.

Scammers could still use the stolen email addresses to contact people they know are 1Password users.

1Password started investigating on Nov. 19 after detecting signs of possible unauthorized access to an employee's corporate GitHub account.

From there, the hacker was able to steal private source code and inject malicious code into 1Password's backend services. The malicious code then downloaded certain administrative data about customers.

1Password publicly disclosed the breach on Nov. 25, six days later.

The company did not specify how many customers were affected or explain exactly how the hacker managed to take over the employee's account.

The stolen data included customer names, login email addresses, account and user IDs, and timestamps indicating account creation and last use.

The hacker also gained access to 1Password's software development and deployment systems.

1Password disabled the compromised employee's GitHub account and revoked the stolen access token.

The company also restored a clean version of the affected service and revoked or replaced potentially exposed internal credentials.

1Password also engaged independent security experts to review its response.

1Password recommends that customers check the 1Password app or type the company's website address directly into their browser if they receive an unexpected invitation or recovery message.

The company says it will never contact users to request their account password or Secret Key.

Update: 1Password claims that there is no need to change one's 1Password account password or any of the passwords saved in one's vault. No customer passwords were exposed in this incident.

Hi CZ! There’s no need to change your 1Password account password or any of the passwords you’ve saved in your vault. No customer passwords were exposed in this incident. We don’t store your account password or Secret Key, and getting into our backend systems didn’t give the attacker the keys to decrypt your vault. The attacker did copy account information for some customers, including names and email addresses, so we recommend watching for 1Password invitations or account recovery emails you weren’t expecting. You can read the full update on our blog: https://t.co/9fbzzAJr0B

#5126. Fidelity Files for Chainlink ETF. What Does It Mean for LINK?

Strict editorial policy that focuses on accuracy, relevance, and impartiality

Morbi pretium leo et nisl aliquam mollis. Quisque arcu lorem, ultricies quis pellentesque nec, ullamcorper eu odio.

Fidelity’s Chainlink ETF proposal would hold LINK directly and trade on Nasdaq if it clears the remaining steps. The proposed Fidelity Chainlink Fund, described in a November 25 registration statement, would use the ticker FLNK, although the filing is preliminary and no launch date or final annual fee has been provided.

The larger question is not whether Wall Street can package LINK. It already has. The question is whether Fidelity can attract fresh demand for the token rather than divide the existing market among another set of fund shares.

The proposed fund would hold LINK, not a basket of blockchain companies or derivatives intended to mimic LINK’s price. Its objective is to follow the token’s U.S. dollar performance, less expenses and liabilities. The prospectus identifies Anchorage Digital Bank, BitGo Bank & Trust and Coinbase Custody as custodians, with the trust intending to hold its LINK on Ethereum.

Fidelity also lays out how the price would be measured. Its proposed reference rate uses prices from eligible LINK spot markets, with a volume-weighted median methodology calculated every 15 seconds using rolling 60-minute market data. That is a mechanism for valuing the assets. It is not a guarantee that fund shares will trade at precisely the reported value when markets are thin or volatile.

Nor is this a yield product. The filing states plainly: “The Trust will not stake its LINK.” Shareholders would not receive staking rewards through the fund. They would be buying securities designed to reflect an underlying token’s price, not a wallet balance they can use in Chainlink services.

That distinction matters because the company’s use of Chainlink technology elsewhere is a separate story. NewsBTC has previously reported on Chainlink infrastructure used with Fidelity’s tokenized FILQ fund. An investment vehicle that owns LINK is not evidence of increased demand for Chainlink’s oracle services, and using the network’s technology does not automatically mean buying its token.

This is not the first attempt to make LINK available through conventional securities accounts. Grayscale’s Chainlink Trust ETF, trading as GLNK, had a share creation and redemption program in place from December 2025, according to its SEC disclosures. The Bitwise Chainlink ETF, CLNK, also appeared in a January 2026 Nasdaq information circular.

And fund shares are not the only conventional route. In November, NewsBTC covered Charles Schwab’s rollout of direct LINK trading to eligible crypto clients. These routes do different things, but they establish a useful baseline: access is no longer the same problem it was when crypto products were confined to specialist exchanges.

Fidelity’s possible advantage is distribution. Its name and brokerage relationships may reach customers who would not open a crypto wallet or buy LINK on a trading platform. That is a credible reason the filing matters. But branding, however recognizable, cannot tell investors how much money will arrive once trading begins.

There is also the price of access. The preliminary prospectus leaves the sponsor’s annual fee blank. Until that figure is settled, it is impossible to make an honest cost comparison with competing LINK products. For investors choosing between wrappers around the same token, fees, trading spreads and the gap between share prices and net asset value deserve more attention than a new ticker.

The mechanics are worth getting right. The proposed trust would issue and redeem large blocks of shares through authorized participants, using cash or LINK under procedures described in the filing. Everyday investors would generally trade the shares on an exchange instead of placing orders with the trust.

Those are two different markets. When one investor sells an existing fund share to another, the trade does not by itself require the trust to acquire more LINK. Sustained net creations can increase a fund’s underlying holdings. Redemptions can do the reverse. A rising share price, meanwhile, may reflect a higher LINK price rather than additional tokens entering custody.

That is why the announcement alone provides no evidence of fresh institutional inflows. The Form S-1 is a plan, not a subscription report. It does not tell us how much outside capital will be committed, what portion might come from rival products, or whether investor interest will survive a difficult crypto market.

There is a fair counterargument. Fidelity could appeal to a materially different pool of investors and grow total demand rather than simply redistribute it. The filing establishes a possible channel for that to happen. It does not establish the outcome.

First, the registration statement must become effective and the proposed Nasdaq listing must move forward. The final prospectus should also resolve the missing fee and other commercial details. Those are immediate milestones, not formalities to be assumed away.

If the product launches, the more revealing evidence will arrive afterward: the number of LINK held, changes in shares outstanding, sustained net creations or redemptions, trading liquidity and discounts or premiums to net asset value. Comparisons with existing LINK funds would help separate fresh demand from investors moving between products.

Until those figures exist, the sensible interpretation is narrow. Fidelity wants to sell investors exposure to Chainlink through a familiar brokerage format. Whether that changes the market for LINK is still an open question, and one that a filing cannot answer.

#5124. XRP ETF Buyers Suddenly Return

U.S. spot exchange-traded funds for XRP recorded net inflows of $4.07 million on Nov. 25. XRP was the only cryptocurrency among the 10 ETF categories tracked in a SoSoValue snapshot shared by BankXRP to register net inflows.

Wednesday's inflows narrowed the net outflow gap for XRP ETFs. Following the latest inflows, XRP funds had recorded $21.25 million more in investor outflows than inflows over the 30 days ending Nov. 25.

That means the net outflows over the rest of the period totaled $25.32 million. In a single trading day, investors covered about 16% of that shortfall.

The five U.S. spot XRP ETFs tracked by SoSoValue currently have total net assets of $1.04 billion. This is marginally higher than the $1 billion held by nine spot Solana ETFs.

However, there is a larger disparity in cumulative net inflows between XRP and Solana funds. Cumulative net inflows total $1.79 billion for XRP and $1.51 billion for Solana.

The two figures measure different things. Cumulative net inflows represent the total amount of money invested in the funds minus redemptions.

Net assets, on the other hand, represent the current value of a fund's holdings. This figure changes with the price of XRP.

This explains why XRP funds have a little over $1 billion in net assets despite attracting nearly $1.8 billion in cumulative net inflows.

Trading activity was slightly higher in Solana ETFs on Wednesday, with total volume reaching $35.54 million, compared to $33.40 million for XRP.

However, Solana ETFs recorded zero net flows for the day.

Investors can trade existing ETF shares with one another without affecting the total amount of money invested in the funds.

The contrast with Bitcoin ETFs was stark.

U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded $123.41 million in net outflows on Wednesday, according to preliminary figures reported by SoSoValue.

However, the total for Bitcoin was still being compiled when BankXRP shared the numbers. SoSoValue marked the XRP total as complete.

With U.S. markets closed for Thanksgiving, XRP ETF buyers have only one more trading day this week.

Trading resumes on U.S. equity markets on Friday, Nov. 27. However, the session will end early, with markets closing at 1 p.m. Eastern time.

#5123. Bitcoin’s Recovery Faces a New Warning After $2 Billion in ETF Outflows

Strict editorial policy that focuses on accuracy, relevance, and impartiality

Morbi pretium leo et nisl aliquam mollis. Quisque arcu lorem, ultricies quis pellentesque nec, ullamcorper eu odio.

The Bitcoin recovery above $60,000 is offering some relief after a brutal November sell-off, but the money flowing through US spot Bitcoin ETFs tells a less encouraging story. The funds recorded more than $2 billion in combined net outflows over four consecutive trading sessions ending November 24.

Bitcoin’s return to the psychologically important price level follows a difficult week in which the cryptocurrency traded as low as approximately $55,300.

The rebound is welcome. What is less clear is whether buyers have returned with enough capital to sustain it.

The scale of the recent withdrawals deserves more attention than the recovery itself.

According to Farside Investors, US spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded net outflows of $582.3 million on November 19, followed by another $669.2 million the next day. Withdrawals continued on Monday and Tuesday, bringing the combined total across those four trading sessions to approximately $2.05 billion.

BlackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust accounted for roughly $1.77 billion in net outflows during that period.

Wednesday’s figures are still subject to final reporting confirmation, although available data points to further withdrawals.

These numbers do not mean that every institutional investor is abandoning Bitcoin. ETF shareholders include different types of investors, from financial advisers and asset managers to individual traders. Some may be reducing risk, while others could be unwinding positions that were never intended as long-term investments.

What the figures establish is that the ETF market has experienced persistent net redemptions, even after Bitcoin’s substantial decline.

That is not the response bulls would ideally want to see from buyers following a major correction.

Earlier this week, Bitcoin fell below $60,000 again after an initial recovery above $64,000 failed to hold.

Glassnode’s November 24 report, titled The Canary in the Coal Mine, documented the severity of Bitcoin’s latest decline. The cryptocurrency reached approximately $55,300 on November 21, falling beneath the lows established during the summer.

That matters because investors who bought during previous corrections may now be sitting on losses despite having entered the market at what appeared to be relatively attractive prices.

Glassnode’s historical data reveals another uncomfortable detail. Long-term holders recently accounted for more than 75% of Bitcoin’s realized losses before their share fell back toward 50%. Similar periods of selling at a loss appeared during previous bear markets, although that alone does not establish that Bitcoin has reached a bottom.

Their behavior becomes particularly important when Bitcoin starts recovering.

Some holders may use a rebound to reduce their exposure or exit positions closer to their original purchase price. Others may be willing to hold through further volatility. Which group dominates will influence how much buying is required to sustain the next move higher.

A price that previously attracted buyers can become an area of selling pressure when the market approaches it from below.

This is one reason why reclaiming $60,000 should not automatically be interpreted as confirmation that the correction has ended.

There is a credible argument against interpreting persistent ETF outflows as evidence that Bitcoin must fall further.

Markets can begin recovering before investor sentiment improves. In fact, waiting for every major indicator to turn positive can mean missing a substantial portion of a reversal.

Glassnode’s latest research offers some historical perspective. Bitcoin’s realized losses relative to capital inflows over the preceding year have reached their highest intensity since the FTX collapse in 2022. Previous episodes of heavy losses have occurred near major market bottoms, but severe selling alone is not enough to confirm that a recovery is underway.

Bitcoin also trades across a much broader market than US exchange-traded funds. Direct purchases, overseas exchanges and other investment vehicles can absorb selling even when American funds experience redemptions.

The distinction is between evidence that a market can recover and evidence that it has already established a sustainable recovery.

Bitcoin’s latest bounce demonstrates that buyers are willing to step in at lower prices. It does not yet establish whether those buyers can absorb additional selling at higher levels.

If Bitcoin begins to hold its gains despite persistent ETF withdrawals, that would itself be an encouraging development. It would suggest that demand elsewhere in the market is capable of offsetting some of the pressure coming from the funds.

For now, the price and ETF data leave that question open.

Thursday’s Thanksgiving holiday adds another complication to the recovery. US equity markets are closed, removing a regular trading session for American spot Bitcoin ETFs while cryptocurrency exchanges continue operating.

The absence of new ETF flow figures during the holiday should not be confused with an improvement in institutional demand.

With fewer traditional financial market participants active, Bitcoin’s immediate price movements may also provide an incomplete picture of how investors are responding to the recent sell-off.

Friday’s shortened US trading session and the subsequent return to normal market hours will provide more useful evidence.

For traders, the important signals are whether Bitcoin can retain its recent gains, whether ETF redemptions begin to ease and whether buying remains strong enough to absorb selling when normal market participation resumes.

The $60,000 level may dominate the headlines, but the more convincing recovery will be the one that can survive without depending entirely on temporary relief from selling pressure.

#5122. Bitcoin miners lose hashrate as hackers hijack up to 1,600 sites

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

On the 25th of November, Bitcoin mining company Braiins warned that attackers had hijacked Bitcoin miners’ work through unencrypted pool connections.

Machines kept running while someone else received credit. That basically left operators paying electricity bills for work credited elsewhere.

Its investigation documented four episodes on the 20th of November, mostly in Europe. Each affected 1,050–1,600 mining sites and diverted 0.6–1.9 EH/s for six to 49 minutes.

Attackers forged internet routing announcements, known as BGP hijacking, to intercept connections and impersonate the pool. Miners reconnected to the same address, making the switch difficult to spot.

Earlier episodes hit Latin America between the 7th and 12th of November.

Responding to an X user, Braiins said the attacks exploited a weakness in Stratum V1, the protocol connecting miners to pools. Stratum V2 contributor Pavlenex added,

This is an attack on MINERS and their infrastructure and is not a vulnerability in Braiins Pool.

The exposed protocol dates back to 2012, and warnings have been issued for years.

Braiins had flagged hashrate theft on the 18th of April 2020. It argued that preventing stolen revenue and reducing operating expenses would encourage upgrades more effectively than decentralization alone.

That history prompted Turtlecute, who works in product marketing at Braiins, to write,

When an X user asked whether this was the first publicly confirmed case, Pavlenex recalled earlier reports of interception attacks.

By November, the financial incentive for upgrading had become harder to dismiss. Braiins reported that miners’ machines showed normal activity while their pool dashboards recorded no credited hashrate.

Six months earlier, seven mining organizations had joined the Stratum V2 Working Group. These included ANTPOOL, Foundry, F2Pool, SpiderPool, Block, MARA Foundation, and DMND.

Reportedly, the organizations represented roughly 75% of the global hashrate at the time. Their backing gave the encrypted replacement substantial reach, but deployment remained uneven.

As of the 26th of November, the official directory listed Braiins Pool and DMND as production pools. It separately listed several solo pools and MARA Foundation’s industrial solo operation.

Foundry remained marked as work in progress, despite reported testing in November. ANTPOOL, F2Pool, and SpiderPool were absent from the production listings.

The exposure extended beyond V2 adoption. Braiins said most major pools’ public endpoints still offered only unencrypted Stratum V1 during its checks on the 23rd of November.

V2 encrypts mining traffic and verifies the pool’s identity, preventing an impersonator from receiving miners’ work. The November attacks showed the revenue consequences when industry support had yet to reach those connections.

#5121. How AI Might Break Crypto: Explaining P vs NP Problem

Disclaimer: The opinions expressed by our writers are their own and do not represent the views of U.Today. The financial and market information provided on U.Today is intended for informational purposes only. U.Today is not liable for any financial losses incurred while trading cryptocurrencies. Conduct your own research by contacting financial experts before making any investment decisions. We believe that all content is accurate as of the date of publication, but certain offers mentioned may no longer be available.

The P vs NP question in computer science pops up in our feeds way more often than it did just a few days ago. No wonder—it's a problem mostly relevant and interesting to mathematicians and computer scientists, and it's also a Clay Millennium Prize problem. It asks a relatively simple question: whether every problem whose solution can be checked quickly can also be solved quickly.

Short answer: no, it can't. P vs NP is an efficiency question. NP is about whether a proposed solution can be checked efficiently, while P covers problems that computers can solve efficiently. For example, solving a complicated Sudoku certainly takes time, but checking the result is not as hard.

The question itself simply asks whether every checkable problem has an efficient solution. P ≠ NP says that some problems are harder to solve than to verify, and that is a core question: most scientists expect P ≠ NP, but proving it is the hard part.

Cryptography is purely mathematical, so issues relevant to computation apply here. ZK-proofs represent a more relevant crypto technology used every day and connected to NP: a statement (such as a transaction) is proven without revealing additional data (a zero-knowledge proof).

But the question is different: could it raise any problems, cause security concerns, or lead to exploits? To some extent—yes. Public-key cryptography is certainly something that can be affected right away—as can blockchains, wallets, and even HTTPS—but P=NP alone wouldn't break the whole industry.

Not really, because you can't change the fundamental math. Even if consensus mechanisms are changed and networks are upgraded, it would be similar to solving 2=2. It's fundamental. But instead of 'solving' it, cryptocurrency projects might adapt to such challenges. New systems might avoid relying on assumptions, so such a change would be a reaction to the consequences.

Quantum computing is a different story. Unlike P vs NP, quantum computing is not just a theoretical question about computational complexity. It's a technological development that could directly affect existing cryptographic systems.
