#5091. Ethereum’s Co-Founder Takes On Crypto’s Next Security Threat. Who Is Vitalik Buterin?

Strict editorial policy that focuses on accuracy, relevance, and impartiality

Morbi pretium leo et nisl aliquam mollis. Quisque arcu lorem, ultricies quis pellentesque nec, ullamcorper eu odio.

Who is Vitalik Buterin, and why is Ethereum’s co-founder now questioning the security of the very devices crypto investors use to protect their wealth? The 32-year-old programmer has turned his attention to a problem that even open-source software cannot necessarily solve: compromised computer chips.

In an essay published on November 26, Buterin argued that cryptocurrency security needs to extend beyond software and into the physical hardware on which it runs. His message builds on one of crypto’s oldest principles, but with a new twist:

For someone who helped build an alternative to centralized financial infrastructure, questioning the manufacturers behind that infrastructure seems like a natural next step.

Vitalik Buterin is a Russian-Canadian programmer, researcher and writer who conceived Ethereum in 2013, at the age of 19.

Born in Russia in 1994 and raised in Canada, Buterin discovered Bitcoin in 2011. He went on to co-found Bitcoin Magazine, where he explored the technology and economics behind cryptocurrencies long before digital assets attracted mainstream financial institutions.

His involvement in Bitcoin exposed him to a problem that would eventually lead to Ethereum. Blockchain technology had potential beyond transferring money, but building more sophisticated applications on Bitcoin presented technical limitations.

Rather than trying to accommodate every possible application within Bitcoin’s existing architecture, Buterin began working on a blockchain designed specifically for programmability.

At the time, he was studying computer science at the University of Waterloo, where he also worked as a research assistant to cryptographer Ian Goldberg.

According to the University of Waterloo, Buterin received a $100,000 Thiel Fellowship in 2014 and subsequently left university to work on Ethereum full-time.

In November 2013, Buterin wrote the initial draft of what would become the Ethereum whitepaper.

The proposal described a blockchain with a general-purpose programming environment. Developers would no longer need to create an entirely new network every time they wanted to build a decentralized application.

Consider a lending platform. Instead of relying on a bank to manage collateral, calculate interest and authorize withdrawals, developers could encode those rules into smart contracts running on Ethereum.

That does not eliminate every risk. Smart contracts can contain bugs, depend on unreliable external data or operate under centralized administrative controls. What Ethereum introduced was the ability to execute financial and other programmable agreements on a shared blockchain.

Although Buterin originated the concept, Ethereum was not built by him alone. Its founding team included seven other individuals: Gavin Wood, Joseph Lubin, Charles Hoskinson, Anthony Di Iorio, Mihai Alisie, Jeffrey Wilcke and Amir Chetrit.

The project’s first live network, known as Frontier, launched on July 30, 2015.

What began as an experimental computing platform eventually became the foundation for much of the decentralized finance industry. Stablecoins, decentralized exchanges, lending protocols and tokenized financial assets now use the infrastructure that Buterin and Ethereum’s early contributors helped establish.

The network’s own evolution, particularly its transition to proof-of-stake and the development of Layer 2 scaling networks, has shaped Ethereum’s first decade.

A hardware wallet is supposed to keep private keys away from potentially compromised computers and smartphones. But what happens if the device itself cannot be trusted?

Buterin’s latest research examines that possibility. He points to supply chain attacks involving tampered wallets and considers the potential for malicious modifications concealed inside apparently legitimate chips.

Open-source firmware allows researchers to examine the instructions a device runs. But those instructions reveal little about whether the manufactured chip has been altered.

Buterin wants manufacturers to disclose physical chip layouts, known as GDS files, so investigators have a reference against which to inspect actual hardware.

The distinction matters. Knowing what a chip is designed to do is not necessarily the same as knowing what the chip inside your wallet actually does.

One approach highlighted by Buterin comes from hardware security researcher Andrew Huang, better known as bunnie.

Huang has been developing a technique called Infra-Red, In Situ inspection (IRIS), which exploits the fact that silicon becomes transparent at certain infrared wavelengths.

Using infrared illumination and suitable imaging equipment, researchers can examine parts of a chip’s internal structure without necessarily removing it from its circuit board.

The technique could help detect substituted components or unexpected differences between manufactured chips and their intended designs.

In a 2024 update on his research, Huang explained that infrared imaging has resolution limits. It cannot reliably reveal every microscopic feature of modern chips. Combining imaging with additional electrical testing could improve confidence in a component’s integrity.

That is an important limitation for crypto investors. Publishing an open hardware design does not automatically make a wallet secure, just as publishing a smart contract’s code does not establish that it is free of vulnerabilities.

Buterin acknowledges that sophisticated hardware inspections are more likely to be performed by specialist organizations than ordinary wallet owners.

His essay is a proposal for improving security, not an announcement that existing hardware wallets have all been compromised.

Despite his status as Ethereum’s most recognizable co-founder, Buterin is not its CEO.

Ethereum is maintained through the participation of independent developers, researchers, node operators, validators and other ecosystem contributors. Changes to the network involve technical proposals, discussion, software development and adoption by participants.

Buterin has considerable influence over those discussions, but publishing a proposal does not give him the authority to implement it unilaterally.

His role within the Ethereum Foundation is also distinct from control over the blockchain itself. In its April 2025 governance announcement, the Foundation described Buterin’s responsibilities as providing technical and intellectual guidance to the wider ecosystem.

His research can influence the direction Ethereum takes. Whether the network ultimately follows that direction depends on considerably more than his endorsement.

Buterin accumulated considerable wealth through his involvement in Ethereum, with much of his publicly visible cryptocurrency wealth tied to ETH.

However, his exact net worth is not publicly established.

Blockchain analytics can estimate the value of assets held in wallets attributed to him, but those figures do not necessarily account for all his investments, liabilities, private assets or holdings at addresses that have not been publicly identified.

They also fluctuate with cryptocurrency prices. A wallet valuation should therefore not be confused with a complete assessment of his personal wealth.

Buterin’s latest essay is part of a longer-running interest in making digital infrastructure independently verifiable.

In September 2025, he published The Importance of Full-Stack Openness and Verifiability, exploring how transparency could extend across the hardware and software underpinning increasingly important parts of people’s lives.

These interests share a practical concern: whether users can independently establish that the systems they rely on behave as intended.

There is a commercial obstacle, though. Semiconductor manufacturers invest heavily in proprietary processes, and designing chips specifically for inspectability can involve performance compromises.

But a device signing a cryptocurrency transaction does not necessarily need the computing power of a modern AI processor. That makes security-focused hardware a potentially useful starting point.

More than a decade ago, Buterin challenged the idea that blockchains should primarily be used to transfer money. His latest work challenges another assumption the industry has grown comfortable with: that trusting the code is enough.

For crypto investors, the next meaningful development may come from hardware manufacturers willing to make their products independently inspectable, rather than another software update promising greater security.

#5088. Chainlink jumps 10% as its Wall Street ambitions gain momentum on two fronts

Fidelity is expanding investment access to LINK as Chainlink develops the infrastructure to keep tokenized financial markets operating around the clock.

Chainlink's LINK token climbed 10% over the past 24 hours to $9.20 as the network deepened its integration with traditional finance.

The rally comes as Fidelity Investments filed to launch a spot Chainlink exchange-traded fund (ETF), a day after enabling direct LINK trading on its cryptocurrency platform.

Meanwhile, Chainlink has expanded its financial market data infrastructure to support round-the-clock trading and lending involving tokenized stocks, commodities and other real-world assets, including during market holidays such as Thanksgiving.

On Nov. 25, Fidelity submitted a registration statement to the US Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) for its proposed Fidelity Chainlink Fund, which would trade on Nasdaq under the ticker FLNK.

The fund would hold LINK directly, with Anchorage Digital, BitGo and Coinbase Custody safeguarding its assets. It would support cash and in-kind share creations and redemptions but would not stake its underlying tokens.

The filing came a day after Fidelity added LINK, AAVE and UNI to its Fidelity Crypto platform, expanding its customers' access to digital assets.

While eligible Fidelity Crypto customers can now purchase LINK directly, the proposed ETF would extend that access to investors seeking exposure through conventional brokerage accounts.

The consecutive moves could substantially broaden LINK's investor base. Fidelity serves approximately 57 million individual investors and reported $7.9 trillion in managed assets and $20.1 trillion in assets under administration at the end of September, making it one of the largest financial services firms in the US.

However, Fidelity is entering a market where investor appetite has weakened considerably.

According to SoSoValue data, Grayscale and Bitwise's spot Chainlink ETFs have attracted $176 million in cumulative net inflows since their respective launches. However, the funds recorded net inflows for just one day in November, putting them on course for their first month of net withdrawals since the market's inception.

Daily net flows for GLNK and CLNK through Nov. 25. Values follow Maketo's displayed rounding and totals are approximate, and non-trading days are excluded.

The slowdown in demand, coupled with LINK's price decline, has reduced the funds' combined net assets by approximately 33%, from $238.2 million at the end of September to $158.6 million on Nov. 25.

Please enable JavaScript to verify and send this form.

Fidelity's extensive retail and financial advisory network could help revive demand, but limited fresh capital could also intensify competition among issuers.

With Fidelity yet to disclose its management fee or launch date, the terms of its offering could determine how effectively it competes with Grayscale and Bitwise for LINK investors.

Beyond expanding investment access to LINK, Chainlink is positioning its infrastructure to capture growing demand for financial markets that operate outside traditional exchange hours.

On Nov. 26, the decentralized oracle network introduced Chainlink 24/7 on its X account, a market data service that extends pricing coverage for traditional financial assets to weekends and public holidays.

The service builds on Chainlink's existing 24/5 infrastructure, which provides pricing for more than $1.6 billion in tokenized equities across six blockchains and supports platforms including Ondo, xStocks, Robinhood, and Coinbase.

Previously, blockchain-based financial applications struggled to value traditional assets when their underlying markets closed, limiting trading opportunities and complicating collateral management.

Chainlink's new service addresses that gap by combining traditional market data during active trading sessions with perpetual-futures-derived pricing when exchanges are closed.

The infrastructure could support continuous trading in tokenized assets, derivatives, and prediction markets, while letting decentralized lending protocols manage collateral risks outside conventional market hours.

Aave, which had more than $34 billion in total value locked at the service's launch, is adopting the infrastructure through Horizon, its institutional lending platform, initially targeting tokenized US equities.

The expansion also affects LINK's economics.

Fidelity's ETF prospectus identifies demand for Chainlink's services as a factor influencing LINK's value, noting that the network converts certain fees paid in fiat currencies and other digital assets into LINK through its Payment Abstraction mechanism.

While Fidelity's expansion creates another avenue for investment demand, Chainlink's ability to generate additional fee-paying activity from always-on financial markets could provide a separate source of demand for its token.

KuCoin will delist Monero (XMR) on Nov. 30, the exchange announced on Thursday. XMR dropped as low as $436 after the announcement and lost almost 15% within four hours, according to Kraken data on TradingView.

In the notice, KuCoin said that XMR would be delisted "in accordance with the Special Treatment Rules of KuCoin." The exchange closed XMR deposits on Thursday and will remove the XMR/USDT, XMR/USDC, XMR/ETH and XMR/BTC pairs at 08:00 UTC on Nov. 30.

KuCoin will also shut down XMR trading bots, Convert swaps and Earn products before the delisting. Users can withdraw XMR until Dec. 31, and KuCoin said that it could close withdrawals earlier if the Monero network stops producing blocks or processing transfers.

On Thursday, KuCoin's XMR/USDT pair had $73.8 million in 24-hour volume, according to CoinMarketCap. It was the largest Monero spot market and accounted for 47% of XMR spot trading. HTX's XMR/USDT pair was second with $29.5 million.

KuCoin did not mention its XMRUSDT perpetual contract in the notice. The contract had $33 million in 24-hour volume on Thursday, according to CoinMarketCap. Binance had the largest XMR perpetual market with $89.3 million.

PerpetualCow, who promotes the Wagyu trading platform on X, also responded to the delisting. "Over 50% of users sourced their XMR indirectly from KuCoin; it fuelled ALL instant swap exchanges," he wrote on Thursday. According to PerpetualCow, instant swap services "don't have their own liquidity" and "simply wrapped around KuCoin and sold/bought into their order books."

In the same post, he wrote that Wagyu had done more than $1.5 billion in volume in less than a year. He also shared a screenshot of Wagyu's XMR-USDC market together with the post, and it showed $63.5 million in 24-hour volume.

Earlier in November, the MEXC exchange also delisted XMR. The exchange removed XMR spot and perpetual markets on Nov. 13.

OKX delisted XMR in January 2024, and Binance removed the coin on Feb. 20, 2024. Binance said at the time that it would conduct a deeper review "when a coin or token no longer meets this standard, or the industry changes." XMR fell more than 15% after the Binance announcement.

Kraken stopped XMR trading for clients in the European Economic Area at the end of October 2024. In August 2025, Kraken announced an XMR delisting for Canadian clients "due to recent compliance requirements in Canada" and disabled trading for them on Sept. 2, 2025.

Of that, a record $7.1 billion came from tokenized equities. That's roughly 3.6% of the quarter's total volume.

Much of the third-quarter growth came from memecoins, according to Bitwise. On Nov. 26, the memecoin platform Pump accounted for $1.29 million of the $2.69 million in daily protocol revenue on Solana tracked by DefiLlama.

For SOL to recover and break even in November, it would need to rise about 34.6% by Nov. 30.

If November ends in the red, even a small decline in December would give Solana a record 10th losing month of the year.

December ended lower in five of the last six years shown on the chart. However, six data points aren't much to base a forecast on.

#5084. Why ECB collateral eligibility could boost demand for tokenized bonds

Past ECB decisions offer clues to the value of using bonds as collateral, while US derivatives exchanges face a different calculation over their Bitcoin holdings.

The European Central Bank (ECB) plans to expand the range of tokenized bonds banks can use as collateral to borrow cash, a move that could lower borrowing costs for issuers and give bond funds additional ways to earn securities-lending fees.

For a borrower preparing a bond sale, the choice of where to issue it could affect the interest bill. From June 2027, the ECB plans to accept qualifying bonds issued on platforms licensed under the EU’s distributed ledger technology pilot regime.

A bank that buys one could raise cash from the Eurosystem using the bond as collateral without selling it. That flexibility may be worth a higher bid at the sale.

Historical bond prices offer a clue to the potential impact. A study of 160 changes in Eurosystem collateral eligibility found that yields on newly eligible corporate bonds fell by 4.6 to 20 basis points relative to bonds still waiting to qualify.

Demand to borrow eligible securities also rose, according to the study. A bond fund could earn a fee by lending the security to a bank that wants to pledge it as collateral. Luxembourg’s 1.7 billion euro ($1.86 billion) tokenized bond already qualified through an earlier route.

Banks bought 47% of the October issue, close to their 51% share of Luxembourg’s conventional 10-year sale in March. Those figures show banks were willing buyers in both markets. As eligibility expands, the more revealing figures will be the yields banks accept on newly eligible debt and how much of it they actually pledge.

#5079. XRP sellers could lose an extra $3,146 on a large trade if five accounts pull their buy orders

Removing five accounts’ buy orders in a simulation cut sampled XRP market depth by 86% and large-sale proceeds by 3.3%.

Five XRP Ledger accounts supplied 72% of one day’s trading volume in XRP against Ripple USD (RLUSD), according to XRPL.to.

For a test of the next day’s order book, CryptoSlate selected the five addresses that led the Nov. 25 session in fills of at least 1,000 XRP, then simulated removing their buy orders.

Funded RLUSD in the first 100 buy offers fell from about 63,925 to 8,805. In the model, the matching pool, a standing reserve of both assets, took most of a 100,000 XRP sale after the removal. A seller would receive about 3.3% less RLUSD than with the full sample.

The last XRP/USD trade on Kraken was $0.94935 when the ticker was checked at 13:07:24 UTC on Nov. 26. On the ledger exchange itself, XRP/RLUSD accounted for 84% of all volume measured in XRP over the seven days covered by XRPL.to’s reconstruction.

In the 24 hours ending at 01:30 UTC on Nov. 25, XRPL.to’s reconstruction counted 25,801 fills moving about 6.3 million XRP. Traders took resting offers from 142 accounts or traded against the automated pool.

The biggest account, whose ledger address starts with rpiFwLYi, supplied 41% of executed volume. Together, the five largest supplied 72%, and the pool accounted for 3%.

A replay through the public trade history endpoint yielded 6.32 million XRP and counted 25,712 fills for the same window, 89 fewer than the published tally.

The index can group multiple executions into one transaction row. In one row covering 525.58 XRP, the validated transaction showed about 514 tokens went to one account’s buy orders and about 12 tokens to another’s.

To test whether concentration persisted, CryptoSlate used XRPL.to records and split combined fills using validated ledger changes.

The comparison covered same-pair fills of at least 1,000 XRP in three 24-hour windows ending at 01:30 UTC on Nov. 24, 25 and 26. The same five addresses, selected by Nov. 25 qualifying volume, accounted for about 71%, 88%, and 79% of qualifying volume, respectively.

The address starting with rpiFwLYi led the middle session, with about half the qualifying volume. An address starting with rURtT5MM led the sessions on either side.

That left the same group with a large share in all three windows even as the leading address changed, and the turnover includes trades in which the addresses gave or received XRP.

The two sides of the XRP Ledger’s order book draw on different inventories. A resting order to buy XRP is funded in RLUSD, which the seller receives. A resting order to sell XRP draws on the seller’s inventory.

The relevant depth for a seller is the RLUSD that buyers can deliver at the displayed prices.

At validated ledger 108584374, which closed at 13:09:20 UTC on Nov. 26, the first 100 buy offers could take about 67,549 XRP at the displayed prices.

Excluding buy offers from the five large-fill leaders left room for about 9,302 XRP in that same sample. The funded RLUSD in the sample fell about 86%.

The matching XRP/RLUSD pool held about 1.99 million XRP and 1.89 million RLUSD. The model applied its standard 0.315% fee and allocated each portion of the sale to the better available price.

The test held the remaining offers fixed and used only the sampled book and the direct pool, with deeper orders, replacement orders, and additional fees outside the simulation.

In the model, a 1,000 sale returned 947.96 RLUSD with the full order sample and 947.87 without the five addresses’ buy orders. At 10,000, proceeds slipped from 9,474.85 to 9,470.90 RLUSD. At 100,000, proceeds fell from 94,197.18 to 91,050.74 RLUSD.

The pool took about 32,451 XRP in the first case and 90,698 after the orders were removed.

#5078. Braiins warns of Bitcoin mining attacks affecting over 1,000 sites

Bitcoin mining pool operator Braiins warned that attackers are exploiting unsecured connections to hijack miners’ computing power and potentially steal rewards.

Bitcoin mining pool operator Braiins has warned of a growing security threat to the Bitcoin mining industry after a series of attacks affected more than 1,000 mining sites.

In a report shared on Wednesday, Braiins said an attacker redirected internet traffic between Bitcoin miners and their mining pools, allowing the attacker to claim credit for work done by someone else’s machines.

The company identified 24 incidents between Nov. 7 and 20, with the amount of computing power affected in a single attack increasing nearly elevenfold over two weeks. “The episodes so far were short, but they grew from under 175 PH/s to 1.9 EH/s in two weeks,” Braiins said.

Bitcoin’s total computing power, known as hashrate, stood at an estimated 1,016 exahashes per second (EH/s) on Nov. 20, according to MineOrNot data. For context, the computing power affected in the largest attack was equivalent to about 0.19% of that total.

Braiins’ report underscores how the widespread use of unsecured connections could leave more Bitcoin miners vulnerable to similar attacks in the future.

Related: Luxor CEO warns of AI ‘dark forest’ following Bitcoin miner hijack

The attacks exploited a weakness in Stratum V1, a widely used mining protocol introduced in 2012 that allows mining machines to communicate with mining pools.

However, the unsecured version does not let miners check whether they are connected to the right pool. This allows attackers to basically impersonate mining pools and collect Bitcoin (BTC) rewards at miners’ expense.

The earlier incidents mainly affected mining sites in Brazil and Argentina. But four larger attacks on Nov. 20 each affected between 1,050 and 1,600 mining sites, mostly in Europe.

While Braiins did not specify whether the attacks affected large commercial mining farms or smaller independent miners, it said the vast majority of Bitcoin’s computing power still uses unsecured Stratum V1 connections.

The attacks come as Bitcoin miners are already facing pressure from lower Bitcoin prices and high operating costs, with several major mining companies pivoting to artificial intelligence (AI) and data center services for new avenues of revenue.

Miners may not immediately notice the attacks because their machines continue to run, the report said. This means they could continue paying for electricity while simultaneously losing mining earnings.

Braiins said neither its mining pool nor the affected machines were hacked directly. The company also did not disclose how much money miners may have lost.

On Nov. 23, Braiins reviewed the largest Bitcoin mining pools and found that most still only offered unsecured Stratum V1 connections.

The company urged miners to switch to Stratum V2, a newer version that protects communications and allows miners to check that they are connected to the right pool.

Meanwhile, miners who cannot upgrade can still use Stratum V1 if their pool offers an encrypted connection and their mining software can verify the pool’s identity.

The warning comes after Bitcoin mining services provider Luxor Technology suffered a separate attack earlier this month.

As Cointelegraph reported on Nov. 16, attackers exploited a weakness in Luxor’s mining management software, Commander, to redirect customers’ computing power to the OCEAN mining pool. The attack affected a little over a dozen customer accounts.

Luxor said it fixed the issue within two hours of detecting the unauthorized changes and also promised to fully compensate affected customers.

#5077. XRP Bulls and Bears to Get 3x ETFs Soon

Two proposed U.S. exchange-traded funds would give investors a way to bet on XRP in either direction, with one targeting three times XRP's daily return and the other targeting three times its inverse.

If XRP gains 5% in a single day, the bullish ETF would target a 15% gain, excluding fees and expenses.

If XRP loses 5% in a single day, the bearish ETF would target a 15% gain.

However, investors betting on the wrong direction could lose approximately 15% of their investment in a single day.

The next update is scheduled for Nov. 30. Following a recent amendment submitted to the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC), the registration statements for these ETFs are now scheduled to become effective on Monday.

The issuer has repeatedly delayed the effective date. It remains to be seen whether the funds will start trading anytime soon.

The filing covers a total of eight ETFs, including bullish and bearish funds for Bitcoin (BTC), Ethereum (ETH), Solana (SOL) and XRP.

Even if XRP's price remains unchanged over multiple trading days, both ETFs could record negative returns.

Since the ETFs rebalance daily, it's important to remember that when the price changes direction, the next day's percentage return is calculated based on the investment's value after the previous trading session.

Let's say XRP rises from $2 to $2.20 on Monday and then drops back to $2 on Tuesday. If you hold XRP over these two days, you'll break even.

However, if you invest $100 in the bullish ETF, your position would close Tuesday at approximately $94.55, assuming the fund achieves its daily target and excluding fees and expenses.

If XRP increases by 10% from $2 to $2.20 on Monday, the bullish ETF would target a 30% gain. Your initial $100 investment would now be worth $130.

For XRP to return to $2 on Tuesday, it would need to fall by approximately 9.09%.

The bullish ETF would therefore target a loss of roughly 27.27% on Tuesday. But that loss would be calculated against your $130 position, leaving you with approximately $94.55.

Of course, the bearish ETF wouldn't fare any better.

#5076. South Korea Moves to Lift Its ICO Ban After Nearly a Decade

South Korea Moves to Lift Its ICO Ban After Nearly a Decade

South Korea is proposing to end its nine-year ban on initial coin offerings, a move aimed at pulling crypto fundraising back onshore, creating jobs and folding token sales into a regulated framework.

The country’s Financial Services Commission unveiled a draft bill, the Act on Digital Asset Industry Innovation and User Protection, on Tuesday that would reverse the prohibition imposed in September 2017, when regulators banned ICOs over fraud, speculation and investor losses.

If passed, it would let domestic projects issue and sell tokens to the public for the first time in nearly a decade.

You can now act on the news you read: Go long or short Bitcoin with perpetual futures, all from your Decrypt Money Account.

Under the proposal, any issuer would have to file a “digital asset white paper” with the FSC before selling tokens, detailing the project, how the raised funds will be used, how many tokens will be issued and the risks involved. Issuers and their executives would face civil damages, financial penalties and possible criminal prosecution for false or omitted information, a liability regime modeled on the disclosure rules governing stock offerings.

The ban, regulators have concluded, never really worked. It largely pushed Korean projects to set up entities abroad and run their token sales through them, with game developers Wemade and Netmarble among the better-known firms that took the offshore route. The FSC’s stated goal is to reclaim that activity and the investment and jobs that went with it.

The ICO reversal is one piece of a sweeping overhaul. The same bill would restrict issuance of Korean won-backed stablecoins to consortiums in which commercial banks hold a majority stake, cap any single major shareholder’s ownership of a crypto exchange at 20% (rising to 34% under certain conditions), extend market-manipulation rules to crypto-to-crypto trades, and organize the market into regulated verticals spanning exchanges, trading, brokerage, custody and asset management.

The shift fits a broader global move toward regulated token fundraising, as the U.S. and others build out frameworks that give crypto issuers clearer legal footing. It also marks a notable turn for South Korea, one of the world’s most active retail crypto markets, which has long paired enthusiastic trading with strict rules.

The proposal is only a draft. It now heads to the National Assembly, where lawmakers must approve it before any of the changes take effect, leaving the timeline, and the final shape of the rules, still to be determined.

#5075. Binance Rethinks VIP Eligibility as Investors Spread Capital Across Traditional and Crypto Markets

Home » Exchanges » Binance Rethinks VIP Eligibility as Investors Spread Capital Across Traditional and Crypto Markets

Binance expands VIP eligibility to include trading activity and asset holdings across external financial platforms.

Binance is adapting its VIP program to recognize financial activity across multiple markets, introducing a new initiative that allows investors to qualify for higher exchange status based on assets held and trading volumes generated on other platforms.

As cryptocurrency and traditional financial markets become increasingly interconnected, high-value investors are managing capital across a growing number of exchanges, investment products, and asset classes. Binance’s new VIP Status Match program aims to account for this shift by allowing individuals and institutions to demonstrate their financial activity beyond the exchange itself.

The initiative is part of a broader series of changes Binance has made to its VIP offering in 2026. In March, the exchange lowered BNB holding and Futures volume thresholds for VIP 1–3, introduced a Holder Program recognizing BNB and Alpha asset holdings across tiers up to VIP 9, and launched VIP Rising Star.

In July, Binance further reduced the wallet asset requirement for VIP 3 from $3 million to $1 million and began counting OTC Spot Volume at four times its value toward Spot Volume requirements.

The exchange also introduced a limited-time promotion running through the end of 2026, under which Stocks and bStocks trading volume counts at three times its value toward the 30-day VIP Spot Volume threshold. The initiative requires no registration and gives regular users and VIP 1–2 members a faster route to the next tier.

The latest addition, VIP Status Match, takes this approach further by allowing applicants to submit evidence of their 30-day trading volume or asset holdings on other digital asset exchanges or traditional financial platforms. Binance evaluates the information against its own VIP criteria to determine the appropriate tier.

Catherine Chen, Head of VIP & Institutional at Binance, said, “In 2024, we started recognizing trading activity from beyond crypto and we continue to refine our VIP Program to better reflect how our users engage across the platform. High-value users today trade and hold across multiple venues, so recognition should travel with them, not stay behind. Status Match does that, while keeping tier recognition tied to clear, measurable criteria.”

Both new and existing Binance users can apply. Applications are reviewed within three business days, and successful applicants receive an upgrade one tier above their qualifying level for 60 days, up to VIP 9. Upgraded trading fee rates take effect immediately upon approval, and participants are assigned a dedicated account manager.

Depending on their qualifying tier, users can also access benefits including VIP Earn, which offers up to 20% higher APR, Capital Connect for VIP 3 and above, customized API limits, sub-account management, and VIP events.

The program builds on Binance’s 2024 VIP Invitation Program but introduces broader eligibility. While the earlier initiative recognized trading activity beyond crypto, Status Match also accepts asset holdings as a qualifying metric and extends participation to existing Binance users.

The additional VIP tier is temporary. After 60 days, Binance will reassess participants against its standard requirements, including BNB balance, spot and derivatives trading volume, wallet assets, and 30-day average net borrowing. Users who meet the thresholds for their upgraded tier will retain it, while others will move to the level supported by their activity.

Through these changes, Binance is seeking to align VIP recognition with how investors allocate and manage capital across the wider financial ecosystem.

Morpho’s largest EURCV vault faces a 13.8 million EURCV liquidity shortfall if its biggest depositor seeks a full exit.

Morpho’s largest listed vault for EUR CoinVertible (EURCV), a euro stablecoin, showed about 13.8 million EURCV less liquidity than its biggest address would need for a full exit on Nov. 26.

A withdrawal would return EURCV to a wallet, but eligible holders seeking euros directly from issuer SG-FORGE would follow a separate redemption timetable.

Morpho’s Steakhouse Prime EURCV vault on Ethereum showed 144.3 million EURCV in deposits and 107.2 million in displayed liquidity, including tokens the app could pull from other lending markets.

The top address accounted for 121 million EURCV (83.8%), according to the same page. Steakhouse Prime was the largest EURCV vault by assets in Morpho’s public ranking.

The comparison assumes the top address sought to withdraw its entire position at that moment. Morpho’s public data show balances by address, which can pool funds for more than one owner.

The European Banking Authority’s Nov. 25 report on stablecoins in decentralized finance found that, in its July analysis, more than half of circulating EURCV was supplied to a Morpho vault.

A standard vault withdrawal draws on idle tokens and funds that can be pulled from the market designated for withdrawals. At Ethereum block 26,500,641, Morpho’s address-level position data put that route’s limit at 103.1 million EURCV against a position worth 120.99 million.

That left about 17.9 million EURCV beyond the ordinary withdrawal limit at the indexed block.

Under Morpho’s withdrawal rules, the app can pull available funds from other markets when the vault configuration allows it, a process called forced deallocation.

Morpho’s withdrawal-options data showed about 102.8 million EURCV idle and about $340,000 available in the designated market, plus about 4 million that could be pulled from other markets, based on rounded amounts.

That last source of funds explains why the app showed more liquidity than a standard withdrawal could use. What a depositor can withdraw depends on what is still available when the transaction executes.

In a lending market where borrowers are using most of the funds, repayments or fresh deposits can free up tokens for another withdrawal.

On eligible vaults, Morpho also offers an in-kind exit that can return some EURCV to the wallet and convert part of the redeemed amount into a direct position in a lending market.

#5073. Bitcoin Miners Go 98 Minutes Without Finding a Single Block

Bitcoin miners experienced their longest dry spell since July on Nov. 26. According to Galaxy's Alex Thorn, it took Bitcoin miners 98 minutes and 19 seconds to find the next block.

That's the third time in 2026 that miners have gone this long without finding a block. The wait ended at 18:28 UTC on Thursday.

For anyone trying to get Bitcoin transactions confirmed shortly after the previous block, the gap meant waiting more than an hour and a half.

Even if you paid a very high transaction fee, you would still have to wait until a miner found the next block before your transaction could receive its first confirmation.

Thursday's gap was the 69th longest since 2011, according to Galaxy Research. It was just three minutes shy of the threshold for the top 50.

And this year's other long gap lasted nearly two hours. On July 6, miners took 112 minutes and 26 seconds to find the next block (number 956,953). That was the 19th longest gap on record, according to Galaxy.

Bitcoin automatically adjusts mining difficulty every 2,016 blocks to keep the average block interval at around 10 minutes.

However,  blocks sometimes are found seconds apart. Other times, it takes well over an hour for the next block to be found.

At any given mining difficulty, the chance that a single attempt to find a block will succeed is incredibly small.

If miners have spent 90 minutes trying to find the next block, the chance of succeeding on the next attempt is the same as it was on the first attempt.

So the expected time until the next block is found is still 10 minutes, even if it's already been 90 minutes since the last block was found. That's assuming the network's total computing power and mining difficulty remain unchanged.

Assuming an average block interval of 10 minutes, Thorn said you could expect a gap of at least 98 minutes and 19 seconds about once every 18,600 block intervals.

That means such a gap should occur roughly once every four months, based on an average of about 144 blocks per day.

Galaxy examined 877,290 block intervals going back to Jan. 1, 2011.

Researchers identified 1,948 intervals where at least an hour had passed between the timestamps of successive blocks.

However, Galaxy flagged 97 of those intervals because an adjacent block had a timestamp that was off by at least 10 minutes. This raised questions about the actual length of those gaps.

The longest recorded interval is particularly interesting.

On Nov. 30, 2011, block 155,290 seemingly marked the end of a 144-minute-and-50-second gap.

However, the miner who found the next block had set its timestamp back by 65 minutes.

After excluding apparent timestamp errors, the longest gap was 141 minutes and one second, recorded on Oct. 13, 2011.

#5071. Switzerland clears 57 jurisdictions for crypto tax data sharing

The move paves the way for Switzerland to exchange crypto tax data with foreign authorities starting in 2028 as part of a global effort to combat tax evasion.

Switzerland’s Federal Council has approved 57 potential partner jurisdictions for the automatic exchange of information on crypto assets starting in 2028, a move that would expand tax authorities’ access to information on taxpayers’ crypto activity across borders.

According to a Wednesday announcement, the approved jurisdictions include all European Union member states, the United Kingdom and several G20 countries. Switzerland will only share information with jurisdictions that express interest and meet international standards for confidentiality and data security.

Switzerland had initially planned to introduce crypto tax reporting requirements in 2026 but delayed implementation by at least a year as lawmakers had yet to determine which jurisdictions the country would exchange information with. Under the revised timeline, crypto service providers could begin collecting data as early as Jan. 1, 2027, with the first exchanges between tax authorities taking place in 2028.

The reporting requirements fall under the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development’s (OECD) Crypto-Asset Reporting Framework (CARF), which aims to combat tax evasion by requiring crypto exchanges and other covered service providers to report customer identities, tax residency and transaction data to tax authorities.

The crypto reporting framework is designed to supplement Switzerland’s existing system for exchanging financial account information and close gaps in tax transparency, according to the State Secretariat for International Finance. Switzerland introduced the legal framework for that system in 2017 and exchanged financial account data with 113 jurisdictions in 2026.

The European Union introduced crypto reporting requirements under the OECD framework in January, with the first international exchanges of information scheduled for 2027. As of March, 76 jurisdictions worldwide had committed to exchanging information under CARF, according to the European Commission.

#5070. Bought Nvidia stock during the 2017 crypto boom? You could qualify for a $290 million settlement

Eligible Nvidia investors who bought shares during the 2017–2018 crypto mining boom could share in a $290 million settlement.

Investors who bought or otherwise acquired Nvidia common stock from Aug. 10, 2017, through Nov. 15, 2018, could share in a proposed $290 million cash settlement if the court approves the deal and their claims qualify.

The parties filed the agreement on Nov. 24, and plaintiffs filed an unopposed motion for preliminary approval that day in federal court in Oakland.

The plaintiffs alleged that Nvidia and Jensen Huang misled investors about how much crypto miners contributed to sales of graphics chips Nvidia marketed for gaming.

They say shareholders suffered losses after the extent of Nvidia’s mining exposure emerged in 2018. Nvidia and Huang deny wrongdoing, and the settlement agreement contains no admission of liability.

The court certified the class in March, covering individuals and entities. Exclusions include the defendants, Nvidia officers and directors at relevant times, certain relatives and related entities, and the defendants’ liability insurers. Investors whose requests to opt out are accepted by the court are also excluded.

Class members seeking payment would have to file a paper or electronic claim by a court-set deadline, with documents supporting their claimed loss.

Under the proposed allocation, approved claimants would share the net fund in proportion to the losses the plan recognizes for their stock transactions.

The plan would use the investor’s documented transactions, including what they paid for the shares and what they received if they sold them, but the court would have to approve the allocation plan.

The net fund would include the cash settlement and accrued interest, less taxes, notice and administration costs, court-awarded legal fees and litigation expenses, and other court-approved costs.

Individual payments would depend on the amount left in the fund and the total recognized losses from approved claims.

The parties accepted a mediator’s recommendation on Sept. 24 and notified the court of their agreement on Oct. 22.

The public docket lists Feb. 4, 2027, at 2 p.m. for the preliminary-approval hearing before Judge Haywood S. Gilliam Jr. in Oakland.

If he grants preliminary approval, the proposed schedule calls for postcard notices to start going out and the claim form to be posted within 20 calendar days of the order. Claims would be due 90 calendar days after the notice date.

#5068. What the CFTC’s New Crypto Reserves Guidance Actually Allows—And What It Doesn’t

What the CFTC’s New Crypto Reserves Guidance Actually Allows—And What It Doesn’t

The U.S. derivatives regulator has quietly opened the door for crypto exchanges and clearinghouses to hold Bitcoin, Ethereum, and stablecoins as part of the financial cushion they’re required to keep, the latest sign of the agency weaving digital assets into the plumbing of regulated markets.

But the fine print matters, and it draws a careful line.

In a staff advisory issued this week, the Commodity Futures Trading Commission’s Division of Market Oversight and Division of Clearing and Risk explained how swap execution facilities, designated contract markets, and derivatives clearing organizations can use crypto assets to meet their financial-resources requirements.

You can now act on the news you read: Go long or short Bitcoin with perpetual futures, all from your Decrypt Money Account.

Those rules require such platforms to hold enough resources to cover at least 12 months of operating costs, a buffer meant to ensure a venue can keep running or wind down safely if it hits trouble.

Here’s what the guidance allows: Certain crypto assets, specifically naming Bitcoin, Ethereum, and payment stablecoins, can now count toward that 12-month requirement, subject to “appropriate haircuts,” meaning their value would be discounted to account for volatility. That’s a meaningful concession, effectively recognizing crypto as a legitimate corporate reserve asset for the firms the CFTC oversees.

Here’s what it doesn’t allow, and this is the catch that defines the policy: Crypto can’t be counted toward a separate liquidity requirement.

Because digital assets don’t qualify as “cash” or “highly liquid securities” under Generally Accepted Accounting Principles, they fall short of that stricter test. In practice, a platform can hold Bitcoin or Ethereum as part of its longer-term financial backstop, but it still needs traditional cash-like instruments on hand to satisfy the rule meant to ensure it can pay obligations quickly.

The distinction is the whole point. It lets firms treat crypto as a store of value on their balance sheets while reinforcing that, when it comes to assets that must be instantly spendable, volatile tokens still don’t make the cut.

The nuance is easy to miss, but it reflects a measured posture from a regulator that has otherwise moved aggressively on crypto.

The CFTC has already previously cleared perpetual futures on individual stocks, issued no-action relief letting crypto apps offer regulated derivatives, and floated a plan to bring crypto exchanges under federal oversight, part of a broader push to set digital-asset policy on its own authority.

That said, it’s worth noting that the advisory represents the views of CFTC staff only. It creates no new rules or enforceable rights, isn’t a no-action position, and doesn’t necessarily reflect the views of the Commission itself.

It could also shift as the agency’s makeup changes. President Donald Trump recently sent a bipartisan slate of nominees to fill vacant CFTC and SEC seats, which could reshape the commissions now steering crypto policy.

For now, the guidance is best read not as crypto winning blanket acceptance as a reserve asset, but as the CFTC sorting out precisely where digital assets fit, and where they still don’t, in the machinery of regulated trading.

The snapshot for Wendy’s is scheduled for Dec. 1, followed by Nvidia on Dec. 2 and Qualcomm on Dec. 3.

All snapshots will take place at 01:00 UTC.

The proceeds will then be distributed among users who hold NVDAB on Binance and qualify for the dividend payment.

The same process will apply to the other four stocks.

If you hold eligible tokens in other products on the platform, such as savings or margin accounts, Binance will still credit the dividends to your spot account.

If you hold bStocks on-chain, the dividend payments will be made by adjusting the token's multiplier.

So if you hold NVDAB, you have an interest in the Nvidia shares held by BTECH.

If you need to transfer tokens to Binance before the snapshot, you must do so at least two hours in advance.

The same two-hour suspension rule will apply to the other four stock tokens.

The exchange will not issue a separate announcement when these services resume.

#5066. Bank of Japan Warns Stablecoins and Tokenization Threaten Financial Stability

Japan's central bank has warned that automated trading in tokenized markets could exacerbate a sell-off.

It also raised concerns about whether stablecoin holders can always redeem their tokens at face value.

A Bank of Japan executive director outlined these risks during his keynote speech at an International Monetary Fund seminar in Tokyo.

In the event of a price drop, according to Kazushige Kamiyama, a smart contract could automatically increase the amount of collateral required. It could also trigger a sale of the collateral backing a position if the borrower doesn't have enough collateral.

These sales could drive prices even lower, potentially spreading financial stress across institutions and markets.

In the case of stablecoins, the question is whether a token with a face value of one dollar can always be redeemed for one dollar.

To ensure this, issuers' reserves need to be properly regulated, and the links to central bank money need to be reliable, Kamiyama said.

A bank might have enough cash to pay for a trade in tokenized assets but still be unable to complete the payment.

This could happen when a trade is settled overnight, and the payment system the bank uses to transfer cash is unavailable.

The bank might have to keep additional cash on a trading platform. Meanwhile, cash held on another network might not be accessible when the payment is due.

"Even with faster settlement, it does not necessarily lead to efficient liquidity management," Kamiyama said.

Cross-border securities trades, however, could benefit from tokenization.

A smart contract could link the payment and delivery of a security so that both transactions are executed simultaneously.

This could reduce the risk of a buyer paying for an asset without receiving it.

The Bank of Japan is setting up a testing environment with financial institutions that hold accounts at the central bank.

One scenario involves exploring how cash settlement could work for trades involving tokenized Japanese government bonds.

The central bank is considering two options for making the cash payment.

One would involve issuing tokenized central bank money. The other would link a token trading platform to Japan's existing payment infrastructure.

These tests will evaluate whether the proposed solutions can address the challenges financial institutions face when settling trades.

#5065. Bitcoin Losses Are the Worst Since FTX. Is the Bottom Near?

Bitcoin Losses Are the Worst Since FTX. Is the Bottom Near?

Bitcoin investors are locking in their heaviest losses since the collapse of FTX in November 2022, according to a report published Tuesday by blockchain analytics firm Glassnode.

The world’s largest cryptocurrency slipped below $60,000, trading at $59,992, more than 50% from its October 2025 peak.

“Bitcoin losses are the heaviest since FTX,” Glassnode wrote on X. “Set against the money that flowed into Bitcoin over the past year, they have almost doubled in a week.”

You can now act on the news you read: Go long or short Bitcoin with perpetual futures, all from your Decrypt Money Account.

Glassnode tracks realized losses by looking at coins that move on-chain at prices lower than when they previously moved. Measuring those losses against the capital that entered Bitcoin over the preceding year gives analysts a way to compare sell-offs across market cycles, even as the cryptocurrency grows in value.

The last time the indicator reached these levels, Sam Bankman-Fried’s crypto empire was collapsing and Bitcoin was trading below $16,000. This time, the selling pressure has coincided with a much broader retreat from risky assets, and even good news for the tech industry hasn’t been enough to keep Bitcoin afloat.

Bitcoin rallied 5% in about half an hour on Monday after Nvidia announced that Jensen Huang was returning as CEO. Less than six hours later, Bitcoin had given back the entire rally, while the Nasdaq 100 still held roughly three-quarters of its gains. In trading, this is known as a bull trap, and happens on strong bearish trends.

Bitcoin’s correlation with the Nasdaq 100 is now at its highest since September 2022, Glassnode said. Over the past 60 trading days, Bitcoin has tended to gain less when tech stocks rise and lose more when they fall.

U.S. investors have also been pulling money out of the market. Spot Bitcoin ETFs have lost $4.3 billion on net over the past 20 trading days, while Coinbase traders have been heavy net sellers over the past month. Buying and selling on Binance, meanwhile, have been roughly balanced.

“Spikes like this often came close to past lows, but some came early,” Glassnode said. The firm pointed to the sell-offs of early 2019, March 2020, and November 2022, when losses surged near market bottoms, but also to earlier episodes in 2018 and 2022 when prices had further to fall.

Long-term holders—investors who have held their coins for roughly five months or longer—accounted for most realized losses from mid-April to mid-November. Nearly 90% of the long futures positions vulnerable to liquidation between last week’s Bitcoin price and $53,200 are also gone, reducing the potential for another cascade of forced selling within that range.

Glassnode is watching Bitcoin’s realized price, the average price at which circulating coins last moved, which currently stands at $53,200. Bitcoin traded below that metric before bottoming in each of the previous three major bear markets.

Applying the discounts seen at the lows of 2022 and 2018 to today’s realized price would put Bitcoin at roughly $41,000 and $37,000, respectively.

For now, the more immediate concern is whether Bitcoin can close above its June closing low of $58,500. Glassnode said a recovery above $60,000 accompanied by renewed ETF inflows would help establish whether the summer lows are holding.

#5064. AI labs likely sitting on cryptography ‘bombshells,’ computer scientist says

AI is driving a massive wave of mathematical breakthroughs which could have implications for cryptography.

(Update Nov. 26 at 11:39pm UTC): This article has been updated to include comments from Quantus founder Christopher Smith.

Theoretical computer scientist Scott Aaronson says leading AI laboratories are likely sitting on undisclosed breakthroughs in cryptography.

In a blog post on Wednesday, Aaronson, a former OpenAI researcher and professor at The University of Texas at Austin, warned that algorithms emerging from AI-driven mathematical advances will eventually break currently deployed cryptosystems.

“I’m virtually certain, from multiple reliable sources, that the AI labs are now sitting on one or more bombshells in that area,” Aaronson said. “However, until I either see details or hear directly from someone at a lab, I feel much, much less confident about the specific nature of those bombshells.”

The remarks add to concerns that AI’s accelerating mathematical capabilities could eventually undermine the cryptography used to secure crypto wallets and blockchain transactions. Ethereum co-founder Vitalik Buterin and researcher Justin Drake raised those concerns in October.

Recent weeks have illustrated the pace at which AI has been able to overcome previously unsolvable math problems.

On Friday, Anthropic mathematician Levent Alpöge released an AI-assisted proof of the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis, one of the most famous unsolved problems in mathematics.

Alpöge developed it with an unreleased version of Claude over roughly six weeks, spanning 17 million lines of Lean code. The proof was later verified as correct by Lean FRO and the Mathlib Initiative.

Days later, both Anthropic and OpenAI released proofs of the VP versus VNP conjecture, described as an algebraic cousin of P versus NP, another major unsolved problem in theoretical computer science.

In October, OpenAI released 722 AI-generated math manuscripts covering 372 problem areas on GitHub, which has since been nicknamed the “mathocalypse.”

“This past week — is very much like I would’ve always imagined the beginning of an AI singularity to look and feel like,” said Aaronson.

Related: AI poses greater threat to Bitcoin than quantum computing, Swan founder says

One of the rumors, according to Aaronson, is that one or both of the AI labs have solved “Factoring in P,” referring to a polynomial-time factoring algorithm — a breakthrough that could threaten RSA cryptography.

However, Christopher Smith, founder and CEO of Quantus, told Cointelegraph that while frontier labs have shown impressive results, there is no proof that factoring or discrete logarithm problems could be solved efficiently.

“These questions are naturally of great interest to anyone who works with technology, particularly in the blockchain industry, since a reduction of security for the elliptic curves could be catastrophic,” Smith said.

Aaronson declined to offer any insight on the idea that ECDSA, a digital signature scheme used by Bitcoin, had been broken.

“Crucially, don’t want the cryptography part of the story to overshadow the intellectual enormity of what’s happening,” said Aaronson.

“If, in these days of long-prophesied revelation and wonders and terrors, your main worry is your Bitcoin wallet, then go somewhere else for rumors about whether or not ECDSA is broken or whatever. I don’t have what you’re looking for here.”
